title.zh: 卷十四 魏書十四 程郭董劉蔣劉傳
title.en: Volume 14: Book of Wei 14 - Biographies of Cheng, Dong, Guo, Liu, Jiang, and Liu
title.raw: 卷十四 魏書十四 程郭董劉蔣劉傳 Volume 14: Book of Wei 14 - Biographies of Cheng, Dong, Guo, Liu, Jiang, and Liu

sentences.zh: 程昱字仲德，東郡東阿人也。

translations.literal: Cheng Yu, courtesy name Zhongde, was a man of Dong'e in Dong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yu, whose courtesy name was Zhongde, came from Dong'e County in Dong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 長八尺三寸，美鬚髯。

translations.literal: He was eight chi three cun in height and had a handsome beard.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi three cun tall and wore a full, striking beard.

sentences.zh: 黃巾起，縣丞王度反應之，燒倉庫。

translations.literal: When the Yellow Turbans rose, the county assistant magistrate Wang Du rebelled in response and burned the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow Turbans rose, Assistant Magistrate Wang Du joined the revolt and put the government granaries to the torch.

sentences.zh: 縣令逾城走，吏民負老幼東奔渠丘山。

translations.literal: The county magistrate fled over the city wall; clerks and commoners bore off the old and young and fled east to Mount Quqiu.
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate climbed over the wall and escaped; officials and townsfolk carried off the elderly and children and ran east to Mount Quqiu.

sentences.zh: 昱使人偵視度，度等得空城不能守，出城西五六里止屯。

translations.literal: Yu sent men to spy on Du; Du and his followers had seized an empty city they could not hold, withdrew west of the walls five or six li, and halted to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent scouts to watch Wang Du; Du's band had taken a hollow city they could not defend, so they pulled out five or six li west of the walls and made camp.

sentences.zh: 昱謂縣中大姓薛房等曰：「今度等得城郭不能居，其勢可知。

translations.literal: Yu said to the county's powerful families such as Xue Fang: "Now Du holds the walls yet cannot live in them; the weakness of his position is obvious.
translations.idiomatic: Yu addressed leading local families including Xue Fang: "Du may hold the town, but he cannot settle there—so you can see how weak he really is.

sentences.zh: 此不過欲虜掠財物，非有堅甲利兵攻守之志也。

translations.literal: "They want nothing beyond looting goods and grain; they do not have stout armor or sharp weapons, nor any serious plan to attack or hold the place.
translations.idiomatic: They only mean to rob wealth and supplies; they lack hardened armor and edged weapons, and they have no real intent to besiege or garrison it.

sentences.zh: 今何不相率還城而守之？

translations.literal: "Why do we not join together, go back, and defend it?
translations.idiomatic: Why not march back as one body and hold the city ourselves?

sentences.zh: 且城高厚，多穀米，今若還求令，共堅守，度必不能久，攻可破也。

translations.literal: "Moreover the walls are high and thick and grain is plentiful; if we return now, recall the magistrate, and hold out together, Du cannot last long and can be broken by fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The ramparts are high and thick, and we still have plenty of grain; if we go back, bring the magistrate into the walls, and stand firm together, Du will not endure—he can be crushed.

sentences.zh: 」房等以為然。

translations.literal: "Fang and the others approved.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and the others agreed.

sentences.zh: 吏民不肯從，曰：「賊在西，但有東耳。

translations.literal: "The clerks and commoners refused to follow, saying: "The bandits lie to the west; there is only east."
translations.idiomatic: The clerks and commoners would not obey: "The rebels are west of us; our only escape lies eastward."

sentences.zh: 」昱謂房等：「愚民不可計事。

translations.literal: Yu said to Fang and the others: "The ignorant masses cannot be consulted about planning."
translations.idiomatic: Yu told Fang and his companions: "You cannot take counsel from a frightened mob."

sentences.zh: 」乃密遣數騎舉幡於東山上，令房等望見，大呼言「賊已至」，便下山趣城，吏民奔走隨之，求得縣令，遂共城守。

translations.literal: Then he secretly sent several riders to raise banners on the eastern hill so Fang and others would see them; they shouted that "the bandits have come," rode down toward the city, and the clerks and commoners ran after them; they found the magistrate and together defended the walls.
translations.idiomatic: So he secretly dispatched horsemen to plant banners on the eastern ridge where Fang could see them; they cried that the enemy had arrived and swept down toward the gates. Officials and townsfolk bolted after them, recovered the magistrate, and manned the defenses together.

sentences.zh: 度等來攻城，不能下，欲去。

translations.literal: When Du came to assault the city he could not take it and intended to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Du attacked the town but could not carry it and prepared to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 昱率吏民開城門急擊之，度等破走。

translations.literal: Yu led clerks and commoners to open the gates and strike hard; Du's forces were routed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yu led the townspeople to throw open the gates and hit Du hard; Du's men broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 東阿由此得全。

translations.literal: From this Dong'e was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Dong'e was saved.

sentences.zh: 初平中，兗州刺史劉岱辟昱，昱不應。

translations.literal: In the Chuping era Yan Province Inspector Liu Dai summoned Yu; Yu did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuping years Inspector Liu Dai of Yan Province called Yu to office; Yu declined to come.

sentences.zh: 是時岱與袁紹、公孫瓚和親，紹令妻子居岱所，瓚亦遣從事范方將騎助岱。

translations.literal: At that time Dai was allied by marriage with Yuan Shao and Gongsun Zan; Shao lodged wife and children at Dai's headquarters, and Zan likewise sent attendant Fan Fang with cavalry to reinforce Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Dai was then linked by marriage to both Yuan Shao and Gongsun Zan: Shao quartered his family with Dai, while Zan detached his aide Fan Fang at the head of cavalry to support him.

sentences.zh: 後紹與瓚有隙。

translations.literal: Later Shao and Zan quarreled.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shao and Zan fell out.

sentences.zh: 瓚擊破紹軍，乃遣使語岱，令遣紹妻子，使與紹絕。

translations.literal: Zan defeated Shao's army and sent envoys to Dai ordering him to send away Shao's family and break with Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Zan shattered Shao's troops and sent word demanding that Dai expel Shao's household and renounce him.

sentences.zh: 別敕范方：「若岱不遣紹家，將騎還。

translations.literal: He separately instructed Fan Fang: "If Dai does not send Shao's family away, lead the cavalry home.
translations.idiomatic: He told Fan Fang privately: "If Dai refuses to pack Shao's kin off the premises, march your horse home.

sentences.zh: 吾定紹，將加兵於岱。

translations.literal: "Once I settle Shao I will bring arms against Dai."
translations.idiomatic: Once I finish Shao, I will turn my army on Dai."

sentences.zh: 」岱議連日不決，別駕王彧白岱：「程昱有謀，能斷大事。

translations.literal: Dai debated for days without deciding; aide Wang Yu told Dai: "Cheng Yu has stratagems and can settle great affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Dai wrangled for days without a decision until his aide Wang Yu said: "Cheng Yu is shrewd and decisive enough to settle this."

sentences.zh: 」岱乃召見昱，問計，昱曰：「若棄紹近援而求瓚遠助，此假人於越以救溺子之說也。

translations.literal: Dai then summoned Yu and asked his counsel; Yu said: "If you abandon Shao's nearby aid and seek Zan's distant help, that is borrowing someone in Yue to save a drowning child."
translations.idiomatic: Dai called Yu in and asked his plan. Yu replied: "To drop Shao's close support and chase Zan's faraway rescue is like hiring a stranger across the river to fish your child from the flood."

sentences.zh: 夫公孫瓚，非袁紹之敵也。

translations.literal: Now Gongsun Zan is no match for Yuan Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan is not Yuan Shao's equal.

sentences.zh: 今雖壞紹軍，然終為紹所禽。

translations.literal: Though he has damaged Shao's army, in the end he will be captured by Shao.
translations.idiomatic: He may blood Shao's army today, but he will end in Shao's hands.

sentences.zh: 夫趣一朝之權而不慮遠計，將軍終敗。

translations.literal: To chase one morning's expedient without weighing distant plans—in the end, General, you will be ruined."
translations.idiomatic: To grasp at a moment's advantage and ignore what comes after is to march straight into ruin, General."

sentences.zh: 」岱從之。

translations.literal: Dai followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Dai took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 范方將其騎歸，未至，瓚大為紹所破。

translations.literal: Fang led his cavalry back; before he arrived Zan suffered a crushing defeat at Shao's hands.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Fang withdrew his horse before he reached home; meanwhile Zan had already suffered a heavy defeat from Shao.

sentences.zh: 岱表昱為騎都尉，昱辭以疾。

translations.literal: Dai memorialized Yu as Commandant of Cavalry; Yu declined citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Dai recommended Yu for the post of Commandant of Cavalry; Yu pleaded illness and refused.

sentences.zh: 劉岱為黃巾所殺。

translations.literal: Liu Dai was killed by the Yellow Turbans.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Turbans killed Liu Dai.

sentences.zh: 太祖臨兗州，辟昱。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor entered Yan Province he summoned Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao took charge of Yan Province he summoned Yu.

sentences.zh: 昱將行，其鄉人謂曰：「何前後之相背也！

translations.literal: As Yu was about to set out a townsman said to him: "How contrary you are, early and late!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yu prepared to leave, a neighbor mocked him: "How inconsistent—first you refuse, now you rush to serve!"

sentences.zh: 」昱笑而不應。

translations.literal: Yu smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yu only smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 太祖與語，說之，以昱守壽張令。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor spoke with him, was pleased, and left Yu as acting magistrate of Shouzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor talked with him, liked what he heard, and appointed him acting magistrate of Shouzhang.

sentences.zh: 太祖征徐州，使昱與荀彧留守鄄城。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Xu Province he ordered Yu and Xun Yu to remain and guard Juan.
translations.idiomatic: During the expedition against Xu Province Cao Cao left Yu and Xun Yu behind to hold Juan.

sentences.zh: 張邈等叛迎呂布，郡縣響應，唯鄄城、范、東阿不動。

translations.literal: Zhang Miao and others rebelled and welcomed Lü Bu; counties answered them everywhere; only Juan, Fan, and Dong'e did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Miao mutinied and threw open the gates to Lü Bu; county after county flipped sides—only Juan, Fan, and Dong'e stayed loyal.

sentences.zh: 布軍降者，言陳宮欲自將兵取東阿，又使氾嶷取范，吏民皆恐。

translations.literal: Men from Bu's army who surrendered reported that Chen Gong meant to lead troops himself against Dong'e and had sent Fan Yi to take Fan; clerks and commoners were terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Defectors from Lü Bu's ranks reported that Chen Gong would strike Dong'e in person while Fan Yi moved on Fan; panic swept the clerks and townsfolk.

sentences.zh: 彧謂昱曰：「今兗州反，唯有此三城。

translations.literal: Xun Yu said to Cheng Yu: "Now Yan Province has rebelled; only these three cities remain.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu told Cheng Yu: "The province has risen against us; we hold only these three towns.

sentences.zh: 宮等以重兵臨之，非有以深結其心，三城必動。

translations.literal: When Gong presses them with heavy arms, unless something deeply binds their hearts the three cities will waver.
translations.idiomatic: If Gong throws his full weight against them without winning their hearts, every one of them may buckle.

sentences.zh: 君，民之望也，歸而說之，殆可！

translations.literal: You are whom the people look up to; go back and persuade them—it may succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: You are the man they trust—go speak for us and we may yet hold the line!"

sentences.zh: 」昱乃歸，過范，說其令靳允曰：「聞呂布執君母弟妻子，孝子誠不可為心！

translations.literal: Yu therefore returned; passing Fan he urged Magistrate Jin Yun: "I hear Lü Bu holds your mother, brothers, wife, and children—a filial son cannot bear such tidings!
translations.idiomatic: Yu rode back. At Fan he urged Magistrate Jin Yun: "They say Lü Bu holds your mother, brothers, wife, and children hostage—the news would crush any dutiful son.

sentences.zh: 今天下大亂，英雄並起，必有命世，能息天下之亂者，此智者所詳擇也。

translations.literal: "All under heaven is in turmoil and heroes rise together; someone destined for the age will appear who can quiet the realm—that is what the wise weigh with care.
translations.idiomatic: The empire is chaos and captains spring up everywhere, yet sooner or later one man will emerge who can still it—that is whom the thoughtful choose.

sentences.zh: 得主者昌，失主者亡。

translations.literal: Those who gain the right lord flourish; those who lose him perish.
translations.idiomatic: Attach yourself to the rising power and you thrive; cling to the loser and you perish.

sentences.zh: 陳宮叛迎呂布而百城皆應，似能有為，然以君觀之，布何如人哉！

translations.literal: Chen Gong rebelled and welcomed Lü Bu so that a hundred cities responded—it seems something might be done; yet in your eyes, what manner of man is Bu!
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong hailed Lü Bu and a hundred districts answered—perhaps it looks promising; still, what do you make of Lü Bu himself?

sentences.zh: 夫布，粗中少親，剛而無禮，匹夫之雄耳。

translations.literal: Bu is coarse at heart, keeps few intimates, stubborn and rude—the daring of a common fellow, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: He is crude inwardly, forms shallow friendships, bullheaded and uncouth—the swagger of a street brawler, not a founder.

sentences.zh: 宮等以勢假合，不能相君也。

translations.literal: Gong and the others joined him from convenience; they cannot treat him as lord.
translations.idiomatic: Gong's crowd rides momentary advantage; none of them can truly serve him as sovereign.

sentences.zh: 兵雖眾，終必無成。

translations.literal: Though their troops are many, they will ultimately accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Numbers will not save them in the end.

sentences.zh: 曹使君智略不世出，殆天所授！

translations.literal: Acting Protector Cao's wisdom and stratagem are unmatched in a generation—surely heaven appointed him!
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Cao's mind and generalship belong to a once-in-a-generation talent—Heaven itself seems to back him.

sentences.zh: 君必固范，我守東阿，則田單之功可立也。

translations.literal: If you surely hold Fan fast while I defend Dong'e, the achievement of Tian Dan can be established.
translations.idiomatic: Hold Fan steady while I shore up Dong'e and we may yet replay Tian Dan's stand.

sentences.zh: 孰與違忠從惡而母子俱亡乎？

translations.literal: How does that compare with betraying loyalty for evil and losing mother and child together?
translations.idiomatic: How can that path rival staying loyal and sparing your family annihilation?

sentences.zh: 唯君詳慮之！

translations.literal: Only you must consider this carefully!"
translations.idiomatic: Weigh it carefully for yourself!"

sentences.zh: 」允流涕曰：「不敢有二心。

translations.literal: Yun wept and said: "I dare not harbor two minds."
translations.idiomatic: Yun wept: "I will never split my loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」時氾嶷已在縣，允乃見嶷，伏兵刺殺之，歸勒兵守。

translations.literal: "By then Fan Yi was already inside the county; Yun went to see Yi, ambushed and stabbed him to death, then returned to drill the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yi was already in Fan. Yun received him, struck him down with concealed blades, and marched his troops back onto the walls.

sentences.zh: 〈徐眾評曰：允於曹公，未成君臣。

translations.literal: (Xu Zhong comments: Between Jin Yun and Lord Cao the lord-minister bond had not yet been formed.
translations.idiomatic: (Xu Zhong comments: Jin Yun and Lord Cao had not yet sealed a true lord-and-vassal tie.

sentences.zh: 母，至親也，於義應去。

translations.literal: A mother is one's closest kin; according to righteousness he ought to depart.
translations.idiomatic: A mother is the nearest of kin; duty said he should go to her.

sentences.zh: 昔王陵母為項羽所拘，母以高祖必得天下，因自殺以固陵志。

translations.literal: Formerly Wang Ling's mother was held by Xiang Yu; believing the High Ancestor would gain the empire she killed herself to fix Ling's resolve.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Yu seized Wang Ling's mother, she took her own life because she trusted that Gaozu would win the world and wished to steel her son's purpose.

sentences.zh: 明心無所繫，然後可得成事人盡死之節。

translations.literal: Once the mind is shown free of distraction one may then fulfill the integrity of giving life for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the heart is cleared of every tie can a man die wholly for his lord.

sentences.zh: 衛公子開方仕齊，積年不歸，管仲以為不懷其親，安能愛君，不可以為相。

translations.literal: Prince Kai Fang of Wei served in Qi for years without returning; Guan Zhong held that one who forgets his kin cannot love his lord and ought not be chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Royal son Kai Fang of Wei stayed years in Qi without coming home; Guan Zhong argued that a man who neglects parents will not love his ruler and must not wield high office.

sentences.zh: 是以求忠臣必於孝子之門，允宜先救至親。

translations.literal: Hence loyal ministers are sought from filial sons' gates; Yun ought first to rescue his closest kin.
translations.idiomatic: That is why wise rulers recruit loyalty from filial households—Yun should have rescued his mother first.

sentences.zh: 徐庶母為曹公所得，劉備乃遣庶歸，欲為天下者恕人子之情也。

translations.literal: When Xu Shu's mother fell to Lord Cao's hands Liu Bei sent Shu back—one who would win the realm indulges a son's feelings.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Shu's mother was taken, Liu Bei released him to her side—aspiring unifiers still honor a child's bond.

sentences.zh: 曹公亦宜遣允。〉

translations.literal: Lord Cao likewise ought to have sent Yun away.)
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao should have dismissed Yun for the same reason.)

sentences.zh: 昱又遣別騎絕倉亭津，陳宮至，不得渡。

translations.literal: Yu also sent separate riders to sever the Cangting crossing so that when Chen Gong arrived he could not ford.
translations.idiomatic: Yu detached other riders to choke off Cangting Ford so Chen Gong could not cross.

sentences.zh: 昱至東阿，東阿令棗祗已率厲吏民，拒城堅守。

translations.literal: When Yu reached Dong'e, Magistrate Zao Zhi had already rallied clerks and commoners and stubbornly held the city.
translations.idiomatic: At Dong'e, Magistrate Zao Zhi had already stiffened officials and townsfolk into a tight defense.

sentences.zh: 又兗州從事薛悌與昱協謀，卒完三城，以待太祖。

translations.literal: Moreover Yan Province clerk Xue Ti plotted with Yu; together they kept all three cities intact and awaited the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Yan clerk Xue Ti worked hand in glove with Yu; the trio of towns survived intact until Cao Cao returned.

sentences.zh: 太祖還，執昱手曰：「微子之力，吾無所歸矣。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor returned he grasped Yu's hand and said: "Without your strength I would have had nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao rode back he seized Yu's hand: "Had you failed me I would have had nowhere left to run.

sentences.zh: 」乃表昱為東平相，屯范。

translations.literal: "He then memorialized Yu as Administrator of Dongping, stationed at Fan.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Yu as Administrator of Dongping with headquarters at Fan.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：昱少時常夢上泰山，兩手捧日。

translations.literal: 《Book of Wei》 records: In youth Yu once dreamed he climbed Mount Tai with the sun in both hands.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei relates that young Yu dreamed he scaled Mount Tai cradling the sun in his palms.

sentences.zh: 昱私異之，以語荀彧。

translations.literal: Yu privately thought it strange and spoke of it to Xun Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu kept the vision to himself as an omen and mentioned it to Xun Yu.

sentences.zh: 及兗州反，賴昱得完三城。

translations.literal: When Yan Province rebelled they depended on Yu to preserve the three cities.
translations.idiomatic: When the province rose against Cao Cao, Yu's stubborn defense saved those three towns.

sentences.zh: 於是彧以昱夢白太祖。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yu reported Yu's dream to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Yu relayed the dream to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「卿當終為吾腹心。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "You shall always be the core of my bosom.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao answered: "You are meant to stand forever at the heart of my counsels.

sentences.zh: 」昱本名立，太祖乃加其上「日」，更名昱也。〉

translations.literal: "Yu's original given name was Li; the Grand Progenitor wrote "sun" above it and renamed him Yu.)
translations.idiomatic: Yu had been born Li; Cao Cao stacked the character for "sun" atop it and rechristened him Yu.)

sentences.zh: 太祖與呂布戰於濮陽，數不利。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor fought Lü Bu at Puyang and several times fared poorly.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao battled Lü Bu at Puyang and repeatedly came off worse.

sentences.zh: 蝗蟲起，乃各引去。

translations.literal: Locusts rose and each side withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When locusts swarmed both armies broke off.

sentences.zh: 於是袁紹使人說太祖連和，欲使太祖遷家居鄴。

translations.literal: Then Yuan Shao sent someone to urge the Grand Progenitor to ally and wished him to move household to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao sent envoys urging alliance and pressed Cao Cao to relocate his family to Ye.

sentences.zh: 太祖新失兗州，軍食盡，將許之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor had newly lost Yan Province and army grain was exhausted; he was about to consent.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh from losing Yan Province and out of provisions, Cao Cao was ready to agree.

sentences.zh: 時昱使適還，引見，因言曰：「竊聞將軍欲遣家，與袁紹連和，誠有之乎？

translations.literal: Just then Yu returned from mission and was granted audience; he said: "I have heard you intend to send family away and ally with Yuan Shao—is it true?
translations.idiomatic: Yu returned from assignment and was admitted at once: "Word says you plan to ship your household north and bind yourself to Yuan Shao—is that so?

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「然。

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor said: "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: "It is," said Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 」昱曰：「意者將軍殆臨事而懼，不然何慮之不深也！

translations.literal: Yu said: "I suppose you fear events as they come—otherwise why reach no deeper counsel!
translations.idiomatic: Yu pressed him: "You sound panicked by the moment—why else settle for such shallow thinking?

sentences.zh: 夫袁紹據燕、趙之地，有並天下之心，而智不能濟也。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao holds Yan and Zhao and harbors ambition to swallow the realm, yet his talents cannot sustain it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao sits on Yan and Zhao with dreams of empire, yet lacks the wit to finish the job.

sentences.zh: 將軍自度能為之下乎？

translations.literal: Do you measure yourself able to serve beneath him?
translations.idiomatic: Do you honestly see yourself bowing under him?

sentences.zh: 將軍以龍虎之威，可為韓、彭之事邪？

translations.literal: With your dragon-and-tiger majesty could you play Han Xin or Peng Yue to another man's throne?
translations.idiomatic: With your dragon-and-tiger presence would you demean yourself as Han Xin or Peng Yue once did?

sentences.zh: 今兗州雖殘，尚有三城。

translations.literal: Though Yan Province is ruined three cities still stand.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Province may be shattered, but three fortresses remain.

sentences.zh: 能戰之士，不下萬人。

translations.literal: There are no fewer than ten thousand fighters ready.
translations.idiomatic: You still command upward of ten thousand seasoned troops.

sentences.zh: 以將軍之神武，與文若、昱等，收而用之，霸王之業可成也。

translations.literal: With your divine martial prowess together with Wenruo and myself gathering and employing them, hegemon-king enterprise can be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal that strength alongside Wenruo and myself and the work of a true hegemon is still within reach.

sentences.zh: 原將軍更慮之！

translations.literal: I beg you to reconsider!"
translations.idiomatic: Think again before you throw it away!"

sentences.zh: 」太祖乃止。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》載昱說太祖曰：「昔田橫，齊之世族，兄弟三人更王，據千里之

translations.literal: 《Wei Lüe》 preserves Yu urging Cao Cao: "Formerly Tian Heng was a great clan of Qi; three brothers reigned in turn and held a thousand li of
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Lüe quotes Yu lecturing Cao Cao: "Tian Heng belonged to Qi's old nobility; three brothers wore the crown in turn and ruled a thousand li of

translations.idiomatic: (Qi—editorial gloss)

translations.literal: territory, commanded hosts reckoned in millions, and stood among the feudal lords facing south calling themselves isolated rulers.
translations.idiomatic: land; they fielded armies counted in millions and faced south among the warlords styling themselves independent kings.

sentences.zh: 既而高祖得天下，而橫顧為降虜。

translations.literal: Then the High Ancestor took all under heaven while Heng in the end became a surrendered captive.
translations.idiomatic: Then Gaozu seized the realm while Heng sank to the ignominy of a bound prisoner.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，橫豈可為心哉！

translations.literal: At such a moment could Heng have borne it in his heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Could any proud man stomach such a fall?"

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「然。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "Indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao murmured: "True enough.

sentences.zh: 此誠丈夫之至辱也。

translations.literal: "That truly is the utmost shame for a man of spirit."
translations.idiomatic: It would shame any man of spirit."

sentences.zh: 」昱曰：「昱愚，不識大旨，以為將軍之志，不如田橫。

translations.literal: Yu said: "I am dull and did not grasp the main drift; I thought your ambition fell short of Tian Heng's.
translations.idiomatic: Yu went on: "Forgive my bluntness—I feared your aims fell below Tian Heng's.

sentences.zh: 田橫，齊一壯士耳，猶羞為高祖臣。

translations.literal: Tian Heng was but one stalwart of Qi; even he was ashamed to become the High Ancestor's subject.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was only Qi's hardiest fighter, yet he blushed at kneeling to Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 今聞將軍欲遣家往鄴，將北面而事袁紹。

translations.literal: Now I hear you mean to send household to Ye and bow north serving Yuan Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I hear you mean to park your kin in Ye and kneel northward to Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 夫以將軍之聰明神武，而反不羞為袁紹之下，竊為將軍恥之！

translations.literal: Given your keen wit and martial brilliance yet you feel no shame ranking beneath Yuan Shao—I blush for you on your behalf!"
translations.idiomatic: With your brilliance you ought to cringe at serving him—I blush on your account!"

sentences.zh: 」其後語與本傳略同。〉

translations.literal: The language afterward largely matches this biography's main text.)
translations.idiomatic: What follows agrees in substance with the standard biography.)

sentences.zh: 天子都許，以昱為尚書。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven made his capital at Xu and appointed Cheng Yu Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor established his court at Xu and named Cheng Yu Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 兗州尚未安集，復以昱為東中郎將，領濟陰太守，都督兗州事。

translations.literal: Yan Province was not yet pacified; Yu was again made General of the Household East of Center, concurrent Administrator of Jiyin, and placed in overall charge of Yan Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yan Province still simmered, Yu was again named General of the Household East of Center with acting authority over Jiyin and supreme direction of Yan.

sentences.zh: 劉備失徐州，來歸太祖。

translations.literal: Liu Bei lost Xu Province and came to submit to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of Xu Province, Liu Bei threw himself on Cao Cao's mercy.

sentences.zh: 昱說太祖殺備，太祖不聽。

translations.literal: Yu urged the Grand Progenitor to execute Bei; the Grand Progenitor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yu pressed Cao Cao to kill Liu Bei; Cao Cao refused.

sentences.zh: 語在武紀。

translations.literal: The detailed account appears in the martial annals.
translations.idiomatic: The fuller story is recorded in the martial annals.

sentences.zh: 後又遣備至徐州要擊袁術，昱與郭嘉說太祖曰：「公前日不圖備，昱等誠不及也。

translations.literal: Later Bei was again dispatched to Xu Province to intercept Yuan Shu; Yu and Guo Jia told the Grand Progenitor: "Lord, when you declined to move against Bei the other day, we truly lacked your foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Bei was sent back toward Xu to block Yuan Shu. Yu and Guo Jia warned Cao Cao: "When you spared Bei earlier, we were simply slower than you.

sentences.zh: 今借之以兵，必有異心。

translations.literal: "Now that you lend him troops he is bound to turn disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: Arming him now invites betrayal.

sentences.zh: 」太祖悔，追之不及。

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor regretted it but could not overtake him in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao regretted the decision, yet pursuit could not catch Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 會術病死，備至徐州，遂殺車冑，舉兵背太祖。

translations.literal: It happened that Shu died of illness; when Bei reached Xu Province he killed Che Zhou and raised troops in rebellion against the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Shu died of sickness first; once Liu Bei reached Xu he slew Che Zhou and openly rebelled against Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 頃之，昱遷振威將軍。

translations.literal: Before long Yu was promoted General Who Shakes Might.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yu rose to General Who Shakes Might.

sentences.zh: 袁紹在黎陽，將南渡。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao was at Liyang preparing to force a crossing south.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao lay at Liyang, ready to ford the river southward.

sentences.zh: 時昱有七百兵守鄄城，太祖聞之，使人告昱，欲益二千兵。

translations.literal: Yu then held Juan with seven hundred men; when the Grand Progenitor heard this he sent word offering to reinforce him with two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yu garrisoned Juan with only seven hundred soldiers; Cao Cao heard of it and offered two thousand more.

sentences.zh: 昱不肯，曰：「袁紹擁十萬眾，自以所向無前。

translations.literal: Yu refused, saying: "Yuan Shao commands a host of one hundred thousand and believes nothing can stand before him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu declined: "Shao fields an army of one hundred thousand and imagines himself irresistible.

sentences.zh: 今見昱兵少，必輕易不來攻。

translations.literal: "Seeing how few men I have he will despise the town and decline to attack.
translations.idiomatic: A weak garrison invites contempt; he will probably march past.

sentences.zh: 若益昱兵，過則不可不攻，攻之必克，徒兩損其勢。

translations.literal: "If my force is swollen he cannot pass without attacking; once he strikes he will surely take the city—both sides only bleed strength for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Doubling the garrison forces his hand: he must assault, will probably carry the walls, and both armies waste strength over a sideshow.

sentences.zh: 原公無疑！

translations.literal: "I beg you, my lord, harbor no doubt!"
translations.idiomatic: Trust the stratagem, my lord!"

sentences.zh: 」太祖從之。

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao accepted the reasoning.

sentences.zh: 紹聞昱兵少，果不往。

translations.literal: When Shao learned Yu's strength was slight he indeed did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Learning how thin the defense was, Shao elected not to strike.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂賈詡曰：「程昱之膽，過於賁、育。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor remarked to Jia Xu: "Cheng Yu's nerve outdoes even Ben and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao told Jia Xu: "Yu's cold nerve surpasses the likes of Meng Ben and Xia Yu.

sentences.zh: 」昱收山澤亡命，得精兵數千人，乃引軍與太祖會黎陽，討袁譚、袁尚。

translations.literal: "Yu enrolled fugitives from the hills and marshes and raised several thousand picked troops; he then led his army to join the Grand Progenitor at Liyang for the campaign against Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu swept up mountain bandits for several thousand veterans and marched to Liyang to join Cao Cao against Yuan Tan and Shang.

sentences.zh: 譚、尚破走，拜昱奮武將軍，封安國亭侯。

translations.literal: Tan and Shang were routed and fled; Yu was appointed General Who Displays Might and enfeoffed as village marquis of Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: After Tan and Shang broke and ran, Yu received the title General Who Displays Might and the village marquisate of Anguo.

sentences.zh: 太祖征荊州，劉備奔吳。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned in Jing Province Liu Bei fled into Wu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jing expedition Liu Bei bolted east into Wu.

sentences.zh: 論者以為孫權必殺備，昱料之曰：「孫權新在位，未為海內所憚。

translations.literal: Commentators assumed Sun Quan would surely kill Bei; Yu judged otherwise: "Quan has only lately taken his seat and is not yet feared throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion held that Sun Quan would execute Liu Bei; Yu disagreed: "Quan's reign is new and the empire does not yet dread him.

sentences.zh: 曹公無敵於天下，初舉荊州，威震江表，權雖有謀，不能獨當也。

translations.literal: "Lord Cao stands unmatched under heaven; his first thrust into Jing shakes the south of the Yangzi. Though Quan is clever he cannot bear that shock alone.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao commands invincible prestige; his opening stroke in Jing rattles the riverlands. Quan may be shrewd, yet he cannot absorb that blow unaided.

sentences.zh: 劉備有英名，關羽、張飛皆萬人敵也，權必資之以御我。

translations.literal: Liu Bei enjoys a heroic name; Guan Yu and Zhang Fei are each a match for ten thousand foes—Quan is bound to arm him against us.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei still carries fame; Guan Yu and Zhang Fei each rival an army—Quan will supply him to shield Wu.

sentences.zh: 難解勢分，備資以成，又不可得而殺也。

translations.literal: Once their interests twist together Bei will be furnished into maturity and cannot afterward be killed at will.
translations.idiomatic: Their positions will interlock: Wu will feed Liu Bei until he is formidable, then killing him becomes impossible.

sentences.zh: 」權果多與備兵，以御太祖。

translations.literal: "Quan indeed furnished Bei with substantial troops to oppose the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Quan duly lent Liu Bei heavy forces to face Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 是後中夏漸平，太祖拊昱背曰：「兗州之敗，不用君言，吾何以至此？

translations.literal: Afterward the Central Plains gradually settled; the Grand Progenitor clapped Yu on the shoulder and said: "Had I ignored your counsel at the Yan Province debacle how could I stand here?
translations.idiomatic: When the heartland quieted, Cao Cao tapped Yu between the shoulders: "Without your voice during the Yan disaster I would never have climbed this high.

sentences.zh: 」宗人奉牛酒大會，昱曰：「知足不辱，吾可以退矣。

translations.literal: "Clansmen brought oxen and wine for a grand banquet; Yu declared: "To know contentment is to escape shame—I may retire.
translations.idiomatic: Kin stacked oxen and wine for a feast; Yu observed: "Contentment shields a man from humiliation—it is time I stepped back.

sentences.zh: 」乃自表歸兵，闔門不出。

translations.literal: "He memorialized to hand back his command and shut his gates, emerging no more.
translations.idiomatic: He requested dismissal of his troops, barred his doors, and withdrew from public life.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：太祖征馬超，文帝留守，使昱參軍事。

translations.literal: 《Book of Wei》 records: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Ma Chao the Wen Emperor remained as regent and ordered Yu to serve on staff.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei notes that during Ma Chao's rebellion Cao Pi held the capital while Yu joined headquarters planning.

sentences.zh: 田銀、蘇伯等反河間，遣將軍賈信討之。

translations.literal: Tian Yin, Su Bo, and others rebelled in Hejian; General Jia Xin was sent to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yin and Su Bo rose in Hejian; General Jia Xin marched against them.

sentences.zh: 賊有千餘人請降，議者皆以為宜如舊法，昱曰：「誅降者，謂在擾攘之時，天下雲起，故圍而後降者不赦，以示威天下，開其利路，使不至於圍也。

translations.literal: More than a thousand bandits offered to surrender; every adviser urged handling them by the old precedent, but Yu said: "Executing those who surrender applied in turmoil when warlords sprang up everywhere—those who yielded only after being surrounded went unforgiven so as to overawe the realm and leave enemies a reason to yield before the siege closed.
translations.idiomatic: Over a thousand rebels wished to capitulate; the council favored the usual slaughter. Yu argued: "Massacring capitulators made sense when the land boiled with rivals—we refused quarter after a siege to cow the realm and tempt foes to yield early.

sentences.zh: 今天下略定，且在邦域之中，此必降之賊，殺之無所威懼，非前日誅降之意。

translations.literal: "Now the realm is largely pacified and these men stand inside our borders; they will surely submit. Killing them frightens no one and abandons the purpose of the earlier rule.
translations.idiomatic: Today the empire is nearly stable and these bandits lie within our borders—they mean to give up. Executing them wins no deterrent and betrays the original logic.

sentences.zh: 臣以為不可誅也；

translations.literal: Your servant therefore believes they must not be put to death;
translations.idiomatic: I therefore oppose execution in this case;

sentences.zh: 縱誅之，宜先啟聞。

translations.literal: even if they were executed one ought first to report upward.
translations.idiomatic: even were we to kill them, His Majesty should hear of it first.

sentences.zh: 」眾議者曰：「軍事有專，無請。

translations.literal: "The assembled advisers replied: "Field command carries discretionary authority—no need to seek approval.
translations.idiomatic: The chamber insisted: "Campaign authority is absolute—no memorial required.

sentences.zh: 」昱不答。

translations.literal: "Yu made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yu held his tongue.

sentences.zh: 文帝起入，特引見昱曰：「君有所不盡邪？

translations.literal: The Wen Emperor rose, entered, and specially summoned Yu: "Do you still withhold something?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi rose, drew Yu aside, and asked: "Is something left unsaid?

sentences.zh: 」昱曰：「凡專命者，謂有臨時之急，呼吸之間者耳。

translations.literal: "Yu answered: "Discretionary orders exist for crises measured in breaths.
translations.idiomatic: Yu answered: "Emergency powers cover dangers that strike between one breath and the next.

sentences.zh: 今此賊制在賈信之手，無朝夕之變。

translations.literal: These bandits are already under Jia Xin's control and present no dawn-to-dusk emergency.
translations.idiomatic: These prisoners already lie in Jia Xin's grip—no sudden peril threatens.

sentences.zh: 故老臣不原將軍行之也。

translations.literal: Hence your aged minister cannot approve the general acting on his own.
translations.idiomatic: An old servant therefore cannot bless arbitrary slaughter.

sentences.zh: 」文帝曰：「君慮之善。

translations.literal: "The Wen Emperor said: "Your misgiving is sound.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi said: "Your caution is sound.

sentences.zh: 」即白太祖，太祖果不誅。

translations.literal: "He reported at once to the Grand Progenitor, who indeed spared them.
translations.idiomatic: He informed Cao Cao, who spared the captives.

sentences.zh: 太祖還，聞之甚說，謂昱曰：「君非徒明於軍計，又善處人父子之間。」〉

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor returned he heard the story and was greatly pleased; he told Yu: "You are skilled not only in military calculation but also in guiding fathers and sons.")
translations.idiomatic: On his return Cao Cao delighted in the tale and told Yu: "You read campaigns—and you know how to steady a father and son.")

sentences.zh: 孫 曉

translations.literal: Sun Xiao
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiao

sentences.zh: 曉，嘉平中為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Xiao, in the Jiaping era, served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiaping he rose to Gentleman of the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：曉字季明，有通識。〉

translations.literal: 《Shiyu》 records: Xiao's courtesy name was Jiming and he possessed broad judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyu gives his style as Jiming and calls him a man of wide discernment.

sentences.zh: 時校事放橫，曉上疏曰：

translations.literal: At that time surveillance commissioners ran rampant; Xiao submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: Inspector-generals of surveillance had grown abusive; Xiao memorialized:

sentences.zh: 《周禮》云：『設官分職，以為民極。

translations.literal: 《Zhou Li》 says: "Establish offices and divide duties to set the people's standard.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou declare: "Create posts, parcel responsibilities, and anchor the people.

sentences.zh: 』《春秋傳》曰：『天有十日，人有十等。

translations.literal: "《Chunqiu Zhuan》 says: "Heaven has ten suns; men have ten ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals adds: "Heaven holds ten luminaries; society stacks ten grades.

sentences.zh: 』愚不得臨賢，賤不得臨貴。

translations.literal: "The foolish may not oversee the worthy nor the low dominate the high.
translations.idiomatic: The dull must not command the wise, nor the humble tower above the noble.

sentences.zh: 於是並建聖哲，樹之風聲。

translations.literal: Accordingly the sages were raised together and their reputations planted like wind through the trees.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the wise were enthroned side by side and their renown spread like wind in the forest.

sentences.zh: 明試以功，九載考績。

translations.literal: Merit was tested in the light and performance reviewed every nine years.
translations.idiomatic: Achievement faced open scrutiny and mandarins faced nine-year audits.

sentences.zh: 各脩厥業，思不出位。

translations.literal: Each cultivated his charge and kept thought within his station.
translations.idiomatic: Every officer minded his brief and refused to reach beyond his rank.

sentences.zh: 故欒書欲拯晉侯，其子不聽；

translations.literal: Hence when Luan Shu wished to rescue the Lord of Jin his son refused to heed;
translations.idiomatic: That is why Luan Shu could not save the marquis of Jin—his heir blocked him;

sentences.zh: 死人橫於街路，邴吉不問。

translations.literal: when corpses sprawled across the streets Bing Ji asked no questions.
translations.idiomatic: when bodies littered the avenues Bing Ji felt no need to interfere.

sentences.zh: 上不責非職之功，下不務分外之賞，吏無兼統之勢，民無二事之役，斯誠為國要道，治亂所由也。

translations.literal: Those above did not demand feats outside one's duty; those below did not chase rewards beyond their portion; clerks felt no pressure to double offices and commoners bore no twin burdens—such was the state's highway and the hinge of order or chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Superiors punished no talent for declining alien tasks; inferiors coveted no prize beyond their portion; administrators wielded no overlapping mandates and peasants shouldered no duplicate labor—that was the royal road to stability.

sentences.zh: 遠覽典志，近觀秦漢，雖官名改易，職司不同，至於崇上抑下，顯分明例，其致一也。

translations.literal: Reading far into canons and observing Qin and Han close at hand, though titles shifted and bureaus differed, in honoring superiors and restraining inferiors and clarifying precedent the principle stayed one.
translations.idiomatic: From ancient statute to Qin and Han practice, whatever the renaming of posts, the aim—exalting authority, fixing hierarchy—never changed.

sentences.zh: 初無校事之官幹與庶政者也。

translations.literal: Originally there were no surveillance commissioners meddling in every branch of government.
translations.idiomatic: Never before had spy commissioners elbowed into routine governance.

sentences.zh: 昔武皇帝大業草創，眾官未備，而軍旅勤苦，民心不安，乃有小罪，不可不察，故置校事，取其一切耳，然檢禦有方，不至縱恣也。

translations.literal: Formerly Martial Emperor founded the enterprise while offices were still incomplete; armies toiled and hearts wavered, so even petty crimes required scrutiny—therefore surveillance posts were added as a rough expedient, yet reins were tight so license did not run wild.
translations.idiomatic: When Martial Emperor laid the foundations, ministries were half-built and the camps groaned; uneasy populations justified temporary inspectors—yet they were leashed so excess never flourished.

sentences.zh: 此霸世之權宜，非帝王之正典。

translations.literal: That was a makeshift for an age of hegemony, not the orthodox canon of true kings.
translations.idiomatic: That arrangement suited a transient hegemony, not the enduring law of sage rulers.

sentences.zh: 其後漸蒙見任，復為疾病，轉相因仍，莫正其本。

translations.literal: Later they gradually won trust and turned corrupt; maladies fed one another and no one corrected the root.
translations.idiomatic: They slowly gained favor, then rotted inwardly; vice fed on vice while the disease went untreated.

sentences.zh: 遂令上察宮廟，下攝眾司，官無局業，職無分限，隨意任情，唯心所適。

translations.literal: They came to spy on palace and altar above while clamping every bureau below—no fixed portfolio, no boundary of duty, acting only as whim dictated.
translations.idiomatic: They took it upon themselves to probe the palace above and every yamen below—without mandate or limit, obeying impulse alone.

sentences.zh: 法造於筆端，不依科詔；

translations.literal: Law sprang from their brush tips without heed to statute;
translations.idiomatic: Edicts flew from their brushes without statutory basis;

sentences.zh: 獄成於門下，不顧覆訊。

translations.literal: verdicts closed at their gates without regard for review.
translations.idiomatic: cases ended on their thresholds with no appeal.

sentences.zh: 其選官屬，以謹慎為粗疏，以謥詷為賢能。

translations.literal: In choosing aides they treated caution as slovenliness and smooth chatter as genius.
translations.idiomatic: They recruited flatterers: steady men seemed sluggish, glib tongues passed for brilliance.

sentences.zh: 其治事，以刻暴為公嚴，以循理為怯弱。

translations.literal: In conducting business they mistook cruelty for impartial severity and regard for principle for cowardice.
translations.idiomatic: They governed through terror: brutality masqueraded as justice, patience for law read as weakness.

sentences.zh: 外則託天威以為聲勢，內則聚群奸以為腹心。

translations.literal: Without they borrowed imperial awe for prestige; within they stacked villains as confidants.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly they draped themselves in divine sanction; inwardly they stacked crooks as intimates.

sentences.zh: 大臣恥與分勢，含忍而不言，小人畏其鋒芒，鬱結而無告。

translations.literal: Great ministers were ashamed to share power with them and swallowed silence; petty men feared their edge and nursed grievances with nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials swallowed insult rather than share authority; petty clerks trembled at their blades and smothered complaints.

sentences.zh: 至使尹模公於目下肆其奸慝；

translations.literal: It reached the point that Yin Mo openly indulged villainy before everyone's eyes;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yin Mo could parade wickedness in broad daylight;

sentences.zh: 罪惡之著，行路皆知，纖惡之過，積年不聞。

translations.literal: notorious crimes every traveler knew while hair-thin faults went unmentioned for years.
translations.idiomatic: flagrant guilt filled the highways yet slender errors vanished from record.

sentences.zh: 既非周禮設官之意，又非春秋十等之義也。

translations.literal: This matches neither the Zhou Li intent for offices nor the Spring and Autumn teaching on the ten ranks.
translations.idiomatic: It honors neither the Zhou model of ministries nor the Spring and Autumn ladder of honor.

sentences.zh: 今外有公卿將校總統諸署，內有侍中尚書綜理萬機，司隸校尉督察京輦，御史中丞董攝宮殿，皆高選賢才以充其職，申明科詔以督其違。

translations.literal: Today ministers and generals command every department without; Gentlemen of the Palace and Masters of Writing administer myriad threads within; the Metropolitan Superintendent polices the capital; the Palace Secretary oversees the halls—all chosen from excellence and guided by written law.
translations.idiomatic: Outside, ministers and colonels hold consolidated commands; inside, palace secretaries and ministers thread policy; the metropolitan inspector guards the capital; the palace clerk watches the forbidden precincts—each seat filled by talent and bound by codified duty.

sentences.zh: 若此諸賢猶不足任，校事小吏，益不可信。

translations.literal: If even such worthies cannot suffice, petty surveillance clerks are doubly untrustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: If those elites still fall short, adding surveillance runners solves nothing.

sentences.zh: 若此諸賢各思盡忠，校事區區，亦復無益。

translations.literal: If each of those worthies strives in loyalty the surveillance corps, trivial as it is, adds no gain.
translations.idiomatic: Should every worthy officer do his duty faithfully, the surveillance corps remains pointless.

sentences.zh: 若更高選國士以為校事，則是中丞司隸重增一官耳。

translations.literal: If instead we elevate national gentlemen into surveillance posts we merely duplicate the metropolitan clerk and superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: Promoting grandees into spy roles only clones existing censors.

sentences.zh: 若如舊選，尹模之姦今復發矣。

translations.literal: If we pick men by the old lax standard Yin Mo's treachery revives at once.
translations.idiomatic: Resume the old lax recruitment and Yin Mo's corruption returns overnight.

sentences.zh: 進退推算，無所用之。

translations.literal: Weighed forward or back the institution has no proper use.
translations.idiomatic: Balancing costs and benefits, the office deserves abolition.

sentences.zh: 昔桑弘羊為漢求利，卜式以為獨烹弘羊，天乃可雨。

translations.literal: Once Sang Hongyang wrung profit for Han; Bu Shi argued that boiling Sang Hongyang alone would bring rain.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Hongyang once squeezed revenue for Han until Bu Shi swore heaven would rain only after Sang boiled.

sentences.zh: 若使政治得失必感天地，臣恐水旱之災，未必非校事之由也。

translations.literal: Were governance's faults truly answered by heaven and earth I would fear flood and drought owe something to surveillance commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: If politics truly moved heaven's temper I would suspect drought and deluge stem partly from these inspectors.

sentences.zh: 曹恭公遠君子，近小人，國風託以為刺。

translations.literal: Duke Gong of Cao kept gentlemen at distance and petty men close; the Airs of the States lampoons him.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Gong of Cao courted sycophants and spurned worthies—the Book of Odes skewers him for it.

sentences.zh: 衛獻公舍大臣，與小臣謀，定姜謂之有罪。

translations.literal: Duke Xian of Wei cast aside great ministers and plotted with petty officers; Ding Jiang pronounced it crime.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Xian of Wei abandoned his council for palace favorites—Lady Ding Jiang called it wickedness.

sentences.zh: 縱令校事有益於國，以禮義言之，尚傷大臣之心，況姦回暴露，而復不罷，是兗闕不補，迷而不返也。

translations.literal: Even were surveillance useful to the state, judged by ritual it already wounds great ministers' hearts; when vileness stands exposed yet the office survives it is like leaving a breach unstitched—lost on a road with no turning back.
translations.idiomatic: Even granting surveillance commissioners some usefulness: by Confucian reckoning the institution already wounds great ministers' hearts; once wickedness stands exposed yet the office survives, it is like leaving a breach unstitched—lost on a road with no turning back.

sentences.zh: 於是遂罷校事官。

translations.literal: Thereupon the surveillance offices were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The court abolished the surveillance commissioners.

sentences.zh: 曉遷汝南太守，年四十餘薨。

translations.literal: Xiao was transferred to Administrator of Runan and died in his forties.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Runan's administrator and died past forty.

sentences.zh: 〈曉別傳曰：曉大著文章多亡失，今之存者不能十分之一。〉

translations.literal: 《Separate biography of Xiao》 notes that Xiao composed extensively though most works perished; surviving pieces number fewer than one tenth.
translations.idiomatic: His unofficial biography adds that most of his writings perished—today's remnants fall short of one tenth.

sentences.zh: 郭嘉字奉孝，潁川陽翟人也。

translations.literal: Guo Jia, courtesy Fengxiao, was a man of Yangdi in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jia, style Fengxiao, hailed from Yangdi in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：嘉少有遠量。

translations.literal: 《Fuzi》 states: Even in youth Jia possessed far-reaching judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The Master Fu relates that young Jia already thought in long horizons.

sentences.zh: 漢末天下將亂。

translations.literal: At the Han dynasty's end the realm verged on turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: As Han slid toward collapse the empire trembled.

sentences.zh: 自弱冠匿名跡，密交結英雋，不與俗接，故時人多莫知，惟識達者奇之。

translations.literal: From his capping he hid his traces, secretly befriended outstanding men, mingled not with the vulgar, so contemporaries mostly knew him not—only the discerning marveled.
translations.idiomatic: After coming of age he effaced himself, bonded quietly with brilliant peers, shunned the crowd, and remained obscure until keen observers marked him odd.

sentences.zh: 年二十七，辟司徒府。〉

translations.literal: At twenty-seven he was summoned to the Minister of Education's bureau.)
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-seven the Minister of Education called him to office.)

sentences.zh: 初，北見袁紹，謂紹謀臣辛評、郭圖曰：「夫智者審於量主，故百舉百全而功名可立也。

translations.literal: Initially traveling north he visited Yuan Shao and told Shao's advisers Xin Ping and Guo Tu: "The wise examine whether a lord measures up; hence every move succeeds and fame may be founded.
translations.idiomatic: On his northern journey he told Xin Ping and Guo Tu: "A strategist sizes his patron—only then do plans land and glory stand.

sentences.zh: 袁公徒欲效周公之下士，而未知用人之機。

translations.literal: "Lord Yuan merely wishes to imitate Duke of Zhou's humility to scholars yet does not grasp the pivot of employing men.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Yuan mimics the Duke of Zhou's courtesy to talent yet misses how truly to wield men.

sentences.zh: 多端寡要，好謀無決，欲與共濟天下大難，定霸王之業，難矣！

translations.literal: He branches everywhere yet masters nothing, loves plotting yet cannot decide—try sharing with him the salvation of the realm and founding hegemony? Difficult indeed!
translations.idiomatic: He chases many ends, grips no core, debates endlessly yet never chooses—you cannot ride such a man through chaos toward kingship!

sentences.zh: 」於是遂去之。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he left him.
translations.idiomatic: So Guo Jia walked away.

sentences.zh: 先是時，潁川戲志才，籌畫士也，太祖甚器之。

translations.literal: Earlier there had been Xi Zhicai of Yingchuan, a strategist whom the Grand Progenitor greatly esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Before him Yingchuan had produced Xi Zhicai, a planner Cao Cao prized.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai died young.

sentences.zh: 太祖與荀彧書曰：「自志才亡後，莫可與計事者。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor wrote Xun Yu: "Since Zhicai died none can debate policy with me.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wrote Xun Yu: "Since Zhicai fell I lack a mind to match mine.

sentences.zh: 汝、潁固多奇士，誰可以繼之？

translations.literal: Ru and Ying surely abound in remarkable gentlemen—who may succeed him?
translations.idiomatic: Runan and Yingchuan still brim with talent—who inherits his place?

sentences.zh: 」 彧薦嘉。

translations.literal: " Yu recommended Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yu recommended Guo Jia.

sentences.zh: 召見，論天下事。

translations.literal: He was summoned for audience and discussed affairs under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao received him and canvassed the state of the realm.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「使孤成大業者，必此人也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "He who completes my great enterprise must be this man.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao declared: "The man who crowns my work stands before me.

sentences.zh: 」嘉出，亦喜曰：「真吾主也。

translations.literal: "When Jia emerged he likewise rejoiced and said: "This is truly my lord.
translations.idiomatic: Stepping out, Jia murmured: "Here at last is the lord I sought.

sentences.zh: 」表為司空軍祭酒。

translations.literal: "He was appointed Libationer of the Army under the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him Army Libationer under the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 〈傅子曰：太祖謂嘉曰：「本初擁冀州之眾，青、並從之，地廣兵強，而數為不遜。

translations.literal: 《Master Fu》 records the Grand Progenitor telling Jia: "Benchu holds the masses of Ji Province with Qing and Bing following—vast territory and strong troops—yet repeatedly behaves without deference."
translations.idiomatic: Master Fu quotes Cao Cao asking Jia: "Yuan Shao grips Ji with Qing and Bing at heel—broad lands, thick armies—yet keeps insulting the throne.

sentences.zh: 吾欲討之，力不敵，如何？

translations.literal: I wish to punish him but lack matching strength—what should I do?
translations.idiomatic: I mean to strike him yet fear I lack the weight—what now?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：〉

translations.literal: "He replied:〉
translations.idiomatic: Jia replied:

sentences.zh: 劉、項之不敵，公所知也。

translations.literal: That Liu Bang could not match Xiang Yu is known to you, my lord.
translations.idiomatic: My lord, you know Liu Bang could not match Xiang Yu in arms.

sentences.zh: 漢祖唯智勝；

translations.literal: The Han ancestor prevailed only through wisdom;
translations.idiomatic: The Han founder won only by wit;

sentences.zh: 項羽雖強，終為所禽。

translations.literal: though Xiang Yu was mighty he was ultimately captured.
translations.idiomatic: for all his might Xiang Yu ended in chains.

sentences.zh: 嘉竊料之，紹有十敗，公有十勝，雖兵強，無能為也。

translations.literal: Your servant privately weighs it: Shao bears ten defeats while you hold ten victories—however strong his soldiers he cannot prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Jia ventures this tally: Yuan Shao carries ten liabilities against your ten strengths—numbers alone cannot save him.

sentences.zh: 紹繁禮多儀，公體任自然，此道勝一也。

translations.literal: Shao heaps ritual and ceremony while you embody spontaneity—this is victory of the Way, one.
translations.idiomatic: Shao buries men in etiquette; you move with natural ease—that is the first edge, doctrine.

sentences.zh: 紹以逆動，公奉順以率天下，此義勝二也。

translations.literal: Shao acts against the tide while you uphold legitimacy and lead the realm—this is victory of righteousness, two.
translations.idiomatic: Shao rebels against heaven's current; you march under lawful banner—that is the second edge, moral right.

sentences.zh: 漢末政失於寬，紹以寬濟寬，故不攝，公糾之以猛而上下知制，此治勝三也。

translations.literal: Late Han government failed through laxness; Shao piles lax upon lax so none submit—you curb with sternness so high and low know restraint—this is victory of governance, three.
translations.idiomatic: Han collapsed from indulgence; Shao soothes chaos with more softness until none obey—you wield severity until order bites—that is the third edge, rule.

sentences.zh: 紹外寬內忌，用人而疑之，所任唯親戚子弟，公外易簡而內機明，用人無疑，唯才所宜，不間遠近，此度勝四也。

translations.literal: Shao seems generous abroad yet jealous within; he employs men yet doubts them and trusts only kin—you seem plain outside yet discerning inside, raise men without suspicion, fit talent to task regardless of distance—this is victory of measure, four.
translations.idiomatic: Shao smiles in public yet suspects his household; kin alone win trust—you seem blunt outwardly yet read hearts inwardly, promote skill without second-guessing—that is the fourth edge, judgment.

sentences.zh: 紹多謀少決，失在後事，公策得輒行，應變無窮，此謀勝五也。

translations.literal: Shao plots much yet decides little and fails follow-through—you seize a plan and execute, adapting without limit—this is victory of stratagem, five.
translations.idiomatic: Shao debates forever yet stalls on action—you strike once decided and pivot endlessly—that is the fifth edge, counsel.

sentences.zh: 紹因累世之資，高議揖讓以收名譽，士之好言飾外者多歸之，公以至心待人，推誠而行，不為虛美，以儉率下，與有功者無所吝，士之忠正遠見而有實者皆原為用，此德勝六也。

translations.literal: Shao trades on pedigree, trades lofty courtesy for renown, so rhetorical flourishes flock—you deal sincerely, advance candor, polish nothing, lead by thrift, stint no reward for merit; upright visionaries with substance willingly serve—this is victory of virtue, six.
translations.idiomatic: Shao buys fame with heirlooms and bowing; flashy talkers rally to him—you spend truth, reward deeds, scorn ornament, model thrift, and stalwarts answer—that is the sixth edge, character.

sentences.zh: 紹見人飢寒，卹念之形於顏色，其所不見，慮或不及也，所謂婦人之仁耳，公於目前小事，時有所忽，至於大事，與四海接，恩之所加，皆過其望，雖所不見，慮之所周，無不濟也，此仁勝七也。

translations.literal: Shao pities hunger and cold he sees and lets pity color his face; what he does not see may slip—mere woman's kindness—you may neglect trifles before your eyes yet on great matters touching the whole realm your kindness exceeds expectation; though unseen your forethought reaches everywhere—this is victory of benevolence, seven.
translations.idiomatic: Shao fusses over visible misery yet misses what lies hidden—that is kindness of the inner chambers—you sometimes skim small sights yet when the empire is at stake your grace overshoots hope and your unseen planning closes every gap—that is the seventh edge, humanity.

sentences.zh: 紹大臣爭權，讒言惑亂，公禦下以道，浸潤不行，此明勝八也。

translations.literal: Shao's great ministers feud for power while slander confuses rule—you guide subordinates by principle so whispering campaigns fail—this is victory of clarity, eight.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's magnates tear at one another through rumor—you steer officers by rectitude so intrigue dies—that is the eighth edge, discernment.

sentences.zh: 紹是非不可知，公所是進之以禮，所不是正之以法，此文勝九也。

translations.literal: Shao confuses right and wrong—you promote the worthy with ritual and correct error with law—this is victory of culture, nine.
translations.idiomatic: Shao cannot fix true from false—you advance the right through propriety and punish the wrong by statute—that is the ninth edge, civil order.

sentences.zh: 紹好為虛勢，不知兵要，公以少克眾，用兵如神，軍人恃之，敵人畏之，此武勝十也。

translations.literal: Shao loves hollow display and misses essentials of war—you defeat many with few, wield arms like a spirit; soldiers rely on you and foes dread you—this is victory of martial prowess, ten.
translations.idiomatic: Shao stages empty grandeur yet mishandles the soldier's craft—you win outnumbered, general like a god; your troops lean on you and enemies tremble—that is the tenth edge, arms.

sentences.zh: 〈太祖笑曰：「如卿所言，孤何德以堪之也！

translations.literal: 〈The Grand Progenitor laughed and said: "If it were as you say, how could I possess virtue enough!
translations.idiomatic: (Cao Cao laughed: "Were it truly so, what virtue could deserve such praise!

sentences.zh: 」嘉又曰：「紹方北擊公孫瓚，可因其遠征，東取呂布。

translations.literal: "Jia added: "Shao is striking Gongsun Zan in the north—exploit his distant campaign and seize Lü Bu to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Jia pressed on: "While Shao fights Zan far north, strike east and swallow Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 不先取布，若紹為寇，佈為之援，此深害也。

translations.literal: Unless Bu is taken first, should Shao raid us Bu would reinforce him—a deadly combination.
translations.idiomatic: Leave Bu alive and he becomes Shao's ally should Shao march south—that danger cuts deep.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「然。」〉

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor said: "Agreed."〉
translations.idiomatic: "So be it," said Cao Cao.)

sentences.zh: 征呂布，三戰破之，布退固守。

translations.literal: They campaigned against Lü Bu, broke him thrice in battle, and Bu withdrew to stubborn defense.
translations.idiomatic: Three clashes broke Lü Bu and he holed up behind his walls.

sentences.zh: 時士卒疲倦，太祖欲引軍還，嘉說太祖急攻之，遂禽布。

translations.literal: The troops were weary and the Grand Progenitor wished to withdraw; Jia urged pressing the assault at once and Bu was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Men flagged and Cao Cao nearly sounded retreat; Jia demanded a hammer blow and Bu fell captive.

sentences.zh: 語在《荀攸傳》。

translations.literal: The account appears in the biography of Xun You.
translations.idiomatic: See Xun You's biography for detail.

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：太祖欲引軍還，嘉曰：「昔項籍七十餘戰，未嘗敗北，一朝失勢而身死國亡者，恃勇無謀故也。

translations.literal: 《Master Fu》 records: When the Grand Progenitor wished to withdraw Jia said: "Formerly Xiang Yu fought seventy battles without defeat yet one reversal destroyed him and his state—because he trusted valor alone and lacked strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Master Fu adds: When Cao Cao hesitated, Jia cited Xiang Yu—seventy victories, then one slip and kingdom vanished—ruined by brute courage without plan.

sentences.zh: 今布每戰輒破，氣衰力盡，內外失守。

translations.literal: Now Bu loses every clash; his spirit fades and strength fails; inside and out his defenses collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Bu loses each engagement; morale gutters and walls crumble within and without.

sentences.zh: 布之威力不及項籍，而困敗過之，若乘勝攻之，此成禽也。

translations.literal: Bu's martial terror falls short of Xiang Yu yet his plight surpasses Yu's—strike while victory runs and he can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Bu packs less punch than Xiang Yu yet sits in worse ruin—ride the momentum and cage him.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「善。

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor said: "Excellent.
translations.idiomatic: "Well said," answered Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 」《魏書》曰：劉備來奔，以為豫州牧。

translations.literal: "《Book of Wei》 states: When Liu Bei came as a refugee he was made Governor of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: "The Book of Wei notes Liu Bei's arrival as a fugitive and appointment as Governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 或謂太祖曰：「備有英雄志，今不早圖，後必為患。

translations.literal: Someone told the Grand Progenitor: "Bei harbors heroic ambition; unless dealt with early he will bring trouble later.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers whispered to Cao Cao: "Liu Bei nurses imperial dreams—delay invites disaster.

sentences.zh: 」太祖以問嘉，嘉曰：「有是。

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor questioned Jia; Jia said: "That is so.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao consulted Jia, who conceded the point.

sentences.zh: 然公提劍起義兵，為百姓除暴，推誠仗信以招俊傑，猶懼其未也。

translations.literal: Yet you grasped your sword, raised loyal troops, swept cruelty from the common people, and summon heroes with utmost sincerity—you still fear too few will answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you drew blade for justice, cleanse tyranny for the people, and woo talent with perfect faith—you already fear empty benches.

sentences.zh: 今備有英雄名，以窮歸己而害之，是以害賢為名，則智士將自疑，回心擇主，公誰與定天下？

translations.literal: Now Bei bears a hero's name; to harm him after he flees to you brands you killer of worthies—then wise men will doubt you, turn elsewhere, and with whom will you settle the realm?
translations.idiomatic: Kill a famed fugitive who trusts your roof and you wear the name of slayer—the clever will flee your banner and who then finishes your work?

sentences.zh: 夫除一人之患，以沮四海之望，安危之機，不可不察！

translations.literal: To remove one man's peril by damming hope across the seas—ponder where safety lies!
translations.idiomatic: Erase one rival by forfeiting the world's faith—that scales survival itself.

sentences.zh: 」太祖笑曰：「君得之矣。

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor smiled and said: "You have grasped it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao smiled: "You read my heart.

sentences.zh: 」傅子曰：初，劉備來降，太祖以客禮待之，使為豫州牧。

translations.literal: "Master Fu states: Initially when Liu Bei surrendered the Grand Progenitor treated him as guest of honor and installed him as Governor of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Master Fu separately notes Liu Bei's first submission: Cao Cao honored him as guest and named him Governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉言於太祖曰：「備有雄才而甚得眾心。

translations.literal: Jia told the Grand Progenitor: "Bei commands heroic talent and holds the people's devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Jia warned Cao Cao: "Bei is born to lead and owns popular love.

sentences.zh: 張飛、關羽者，皆萬人之敵也，為之死用。

translations.literal: Zhang Fei and Guan Yu are each worth ten thousand foes and die for him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei and Guan Yu match legions apiece and spend their lives for him.

sentences.zh: 嘉觀之，備終不為人下，其謀未可測也。

translations.literal: In Jia's observation Bei will never serve beneath another; his designs cannot be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: Jia judged that Bei would kneel to no master—his plots ran beyond sight.

sentences.zh: 古人有言：'一日縱敵，數世之患。

translations.literal: The ancients said: 'Spare an enemy one day and generations suffer.
translations.idiomatic: The proverb runs: spare a foe one dawn and heirs pay for ages.

sentences.zh: '宜早為之所。

translations.literal: 'Deal with him early.
translations.idiomatic: Strike him now.

sentences.zh: 」是時，太祖奉天子以號令天下，方招懷英雄以明大信，未得從嘉謀。

translations.literal: "At that moment the Grand Progenitor upheld the Son of Heaven to command the realm and courted heroes to broadcast great faith—he could not heed Jia's scheme.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Cao Cao carried the emperor's mandate and courted fame through mercy—Jia's counsel went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 會太祖使備要擊袁術，嘉與程昱俱駕而諫太祖曰：「放備，變作矣！

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor dispatched Bei to intercept Yuan Shu, Jia with Cheng Yu rode together to remonstrate: "Release Bei and mutiny follows!
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao sent Bei against Yuan Shu, Jia and Yu drove alongside him: "Let Liu Bei ride off and rebellion blooms!

sentences.zh: 」時備已去，遂舉兵以叛。

translations.literal: "By then Bei had already departed and soon raised troops in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Bei had already gone; shortly he hoisted arms.

sentences.zh: 太祖恨不用嘉之言。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor regretted not employing Jia's words.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao rued ignoring Jia.

sentences.zh: 案《魏書》所云，與《傅子》正反也。〉

translations.literal: Note the 《Book of Wei》 passage contradicts 《Master Fu》 point for point.)
translations.idiomatic: Pei observes that the Book of Wei and Master Fu flatly contradict each other.)

sentences.zh: 孫策轉鬪千里，盡有江東，聞太祖與袁紹相持於官渡，將渡江北襲許。

translations.literal: Sun Ce fought his way a thousand li until all lands east of the Yangzi were his; hearing the Grand Progenitor locked with Yuan Shao at Guandu he planned to ford north and raid Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce carved a thousand li through Wu until the eastern river was his; learning Cao Cao dueled Yuan Shao at Guandu he prepared to cross north against Xu.

sentences.zh: 眾聞皆懼，嘉料之曰：「策新並江東，所誅皆英豪雄傑，能得人死力者也。

translations.literal: All who heard were afraid; Jia judged: "Ce has newly annexed Jiangdong and executed every champion there—men who could inspire devotion unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread until Jia observed: "Ce freshly swallowed Wu and butchered its stalwarts—fighters who inspire suicidal loyalty.

sentences.zh: 然策輕而無備，雖有百萬之眾，無異於獨行中原也。

translations.literal: Yet Ce is reckless and unprepared; though he leads a million he might as well wander the Central Plains alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ce courts danger bareheaded—a million men cannot armor rashness.

sentences.zh: 若刺客伏起，一人之敵耳。

translations.literal: Were assassins to spring from hiding he would face but a single foe.
translations.idiomatic: A lone blade in ambush ends him.

sentences.zh: 以吾觀之，必死於匹夫之手。

translations.literal: In my view he will die at some commoner's hand.
translations.idiomatic: Jia wagered he would fall to a nobody.

sentences.zh: 」策臨江未濟，果為許貢客所殺。

translations.literal: "Ce reached the riverbank before crossing and was indeed slain by retainers of Xu Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Ce died on the bank before he crossed—Xu Gong's avengers cut him down.

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：太祖欲速征劉備，議者懼軍出，袁紹擊其後，進不得戰而退失所據。

translations.literal: 《Master Fu》 records: The Grand Progenitor wished to march swiftly against Liu Bei; advisers feared leaving camp would let Yuan Shao strike the rear—unable to fight forward yet forfeiting position.
translations.idiomatic: Master Fu notes Cao Cao's urge to rush Bei while ministers dreaded Yuan Shao's hammer from behind—stuck between battle and base.

sentences.zh: 語在《武紀》。

translations.literal: The account appears in the martial annals.
translations.idiomatic: Details sit in the martial annals.

sentences.zh: 太祖疑，以問嘉。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor hesitated and questioned Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wavered and put it to Jia.

sentences.zh: 嘉勸太祖曰：「紹性遲而多疑，來必不速。

translations.literal: Jia urged the Grand Progenitor: "Shao is sluggish by nature and suspicious—when he moves he will not be swift.
translations.idiomatic: Jia argued: "Shao moves slow and doubts every shadow—he will arrive late.

sentences.zh: 備新起，眾心未附，急擊之必敗。

translations.literal: Bei is newly risen and hearts are not yet bound to him; strike hard and he must collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Bei's following is fresh—hit fast and he shatters.

sentences.zh: 此存亡之機，不可失也。

translations.literal: This is the hinge of survival—do not miss it.
translations.idiomatic: That moment decides whether you endure—let it not slip.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「善。

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor said: "Excellent.
translations.idiomatic: "Agreed," said Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 」遂東征備。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he marched east against Bei.
translations.idiomatic: He drove east against Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 備敗奔紹，紹果不出。

translations.literal: Bei was defeated and fled to Shao; Shao indeed did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Bei broke and ran to Yuan Shao; Shao never left his camps.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案武紀，決計征備，量紹不出，皆出自太祖。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi notes that according to the martial annals the resolve to campaign against Bei and the calculation that Shao would stay home both issued from the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi counters that the martial annals credit Cao Cao alone with deciding to strike Bei and predicting Shao's inertia.

sentences.zh: 此云用嘉計，則為不同。

translations.literal: To say Jia supplied the plan differs.
translations.idiomatic: Attributing the stratagem to Jia conflicts with that record.

sentences.zh: 又本傳稱

translations.literal: Moreover the main biography states
translations.idiomatic: The standard memoir adds

translations.literal: (from)
translations.idiomatic: (supplied word 'from')

sentences.zh: 嘉料孫策輕佻，必死於匹夫之手，誠為明於見事。

translations.literal: that Jia gauged Sun Ce as reckless and doomed to die by a commoner—truly clear-sighted.
translations.idiomatic: that Jia sized Sun Ce as rash and certain to perish at vulgar hands—acute prophecy indeed.

sentences.zh: 然自非上智，無以知其死在何年也。

translations.literal: Yet unless one is foremost in wisdom none can know which year holds his death.
translations.idiomatic: Only the sage could pin the calendar year of that death.

sentences.zh: 今正以襲許年死，此蓋事之偶合。〉

translations.literal: Now because he happened to die the year of the Xu raid people treat it as neat coincidence.)
translations.idiomatic: Because fate placed his death in the Xu raid year later readers mistake coincidence for foresight.)

sentences.zh: 從破袁紹，紹死，又從討譚、尚於黎陽，連戰數克。

translations.literal: He followed in destroying Yuan Shao; after Shao's death he joined the punitive march against Tan and Shang at Liyang, winning repeated battles.
translations.idiomatic: He aided the ruin of Yuan Shao; when Shao died he joined the Liyang push against Tan and Shang, stacking victories.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲乘勝遂攻之，嘉曰：「袁紹愛此二子，莫適立也。

translations.literal: The generals wished to exploit victory and press the attack; Jia said: "Yuan Shao loved these two sons and could not choose an heir.
translations.idiomatic: Generals hungered to chase the rout; Jia counseled: "Shao adored both sons and never picked one successor.

sentences.zh: 有郭圖、逢紀為之謀臣，必交鬥其間，還相離也。

translations.literal: With Guo Tu and Feng Ji as strategists they are bound to intrigue against each other until estrangement grows.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tu and Feng Ji will pit brother against brother until hatred ripens.

sentences.zh: 急之則相持，緩之而後爭心生。

translations.literal: Press them and they cling together; slacken and rivalry stirs.
translations.idiomatic: Hurry them and they unite; slacken and ambition divides them.

sentences.zh: 不如南向荊州若征劉表者，以待其變；

translations.literal: Better feign a southern drive on Jing Province as though campaigning against Liu Biao and await their rupture;
translations.idiomatic: Better mime a march on Jing as if hunting Liu Biao and watch them tear apart;

sentences.zh: 變成而後擊之，可一舉定也。

translations.literal: once change comes strike and you may settle all at one blow.
translations.idiomatic: when the crack widens, one blow finishes the north.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「善。

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor said: "Excellent.
translations.idiomatic: "Sound," said Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 」乃南征。

translations.literal: "He therefore marched south.
translations.idiomatic: He pivoted south.

sentences.zh: 軍至西平，譚、尚果爭冀州。

translations.literal: When the army reached Xiping Tan and Shang indeed quarreled over Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiping the Yuan brothers warred for Ji.

sentences.zh: 譚為尚軍所敗，走保平原，遣辛毗乞降。

translations.literal: Tan was beaten by Shang's army, fled to defend Pingyuan, and sent Xin Pi to beg surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Tan fled Shang's assault to Pingyuan and dispatched Xin Pi to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 太祖還救之，遂從定鄴。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor turned back to rescue him and thereafter followed through in pacifying Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wheeled north to rescue him and soon sealed Ye.

sentences.zh: 又從攻譚於南皮，冀州平。

translations.literal: He next joined the assault on Tan at Nanpi and pacified Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He helped storm Nanpi and quiet Ji.

sentences.zh: 封嘉洧陽亭侯。

translations.literal: Jia was enfeoffed village marquis of Weiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jia took the village marquisate of Weiyang.

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：河北既平，太祖多辟召青、冀、幽、并知名之士，漸臣使之，以為省事掾屬。

translations.literal: 《Master Fu》 records: After Hebei submitted the Grand Progenitor widely summoned noted gentlemen of Qing, Ji, You, and Bing, gradually employing them as clerks for administrative convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Master Fu adds that once Hebei fell Cao Cao drafted luminaries of four provinces into secretarial posts—that scheme was Jia's.

sentences.zh: 皆嘉之謀也。〉

translations.literal: All were Jia's stratagem.)
translations.idiomatic: Every one of those appointments traced to Jia.)

sentences.zh: 太祖將征袁尚及三郡烏丸，諸下多懼劉表使劉備襲許以討太祖，嘉曰：

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor prepared to campaign against Yuan Shang and the Wuhuan of three commanderies many subordinates feared Liu Biao would send Liu Bei to raid Xu and strike the Grand Progenitor; Jia said:
translations.idiomatic: As Cao Cao readied war on Shang and the three Wuhuan cantons his staff dreaded Liu Biao dispatching Liu Bei against Xu; Jia answered:

sentences.zh: 公雖威震天下，胡恃其遠，必不設備。

translations.literal: Though you awe the realm the Hu trust their remoteness and will not prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians bank on distance—they will not brace for you.

sentences.zh: 因其無備，卒然擊之，可破滅也。

translations.literal: Exploit their unreadiness: strike suddenly and you can annihilate them.
translations.idiomatic: Catch them lounging and a sudden blow wipes them out.

sentences.zh: 且袁紹有恩於民夷，而尚兄弟生存。

translations.literal: Moreover Yuan Shao won kindness among tribes and commoners while Shang's brothers still live.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao's kindness still haunts the frontier and his sons breathe.

sentences.zh: 今四州之民，徒以威附，德施未加，舍而南征，尚因烏丸之資，招其死主之臣，胡人一動，民夷俱應，以生蹋頓之心，成覬覦之計，恐青、冀非己之有也。

translations.literal: Now the folk of four provinces cling only from fear; kindness has not yet touched them—abandon that for a southern expedition and Shang will leverage Wuhuan stores to rally death-sworn followers; once the Hu stir both tribes and settlers may answer, feeding Tadun's ambition and schemes of usurpation—Qing and Ji may cease to be yours.
translations.idiomatic: Four provinces obey terror alone—grace never landed; march south now and Shang trades Wuhuan grain for fanatics; nomads twitch, settlers rise, Tadun dreams of kingship, and Qing plus Ji slip from your grasp.

sentences.zh: 表，坐談客耳，自知才不足以御備，重任之則恐不能制，輕任之則備不為用，雖虛國遠征，公無憂矣。

translations.literal: Biao is a salon debater who knows his talents cannot harness Bei—empower Bei heavily and he fears losing control; empower lightly and Bei will not serve—though you empty the heartland on a distant march you need not worry.
translations.idiomatic: Biao talks philosophy yet knows he cannot leash Bei—give Bei power and he risks coup, withhold it and Bei sulks—strip the capital bare if you must; Biao will not move.

sentences.zh: 太祖遂行。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor then proceeded.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao marched.

sentences.zh: 至易，嘉言曰：「兵貴神速。

translations.literal: Reaching Yi Jia declared: "Victory belongs to the swift.
translations.idiomatic: At Yi Jia insisted speed wins wars.

sentences.zh: 今千里襲人，輜重多，難以趣利，且彼聞之，必為備；
