translations.literal: Now a thousand-li raid burdened with baggage cannot seize advantage; moreover the enemy will hear and prepare;
translations.idiomatic: A thousand-li strike weighed down with wagons forfeits surprise—news travels and defenses rise;

sentences.zh: 不如留輜重，輕兵兼道以出，掩其不意。

translations.literal: better leave baggage and drive light troops by forced march to catch them unaware.
translations.idiomatic: drop the trains, sprint lean columns, strike before they blink.

sentences.zh: 」太祖乃密出盧龍塞，直指單于庭。

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor secretly exited Lulong Pass straight toward the Shanyu's court.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao stole through Lulong Pass toward the chieftain's yurt.

sentences.zh: 虜卒聞太祖至，惶怖合戰。

translations.literal: The captives heard the Grand Progenitor had come and in panic joined battle.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes learned he arrived and collided with him in terror.

sentences.zh: 大破之，斬蹋頓及名王已下。

translations.literal: They inflicted a great defeat, beheading Tadun and the ranked kings beneath him.
translations.idiomatic: The army routed the host, executing Tadun and the leading tribal kings.

sentences.zh: 尚及兄熙走遼東。

translations.literal: Shang together with his elder brother Xi fled to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang and Yuan Xi raced into Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 董昭字公仁，濟陰定陶人也。

translations.literal: Dong Zhao, courtesy Gongren, was a man of Dingtao in Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhao, whose courtesy name was Gongren, came from Dingtao in Jiyin Commandery.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，除癭陶長、柏人令，袁紹以為參軍事。

translations.literal: Recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, he was appointed magistrate of Yingtao and Bairen; Yuan Shao employed him on military staff.
translations.idiomatic: Raised as Filial and Honest, he served as magistrate of Yingtao and Bairen before Yuan Shao took him onto staff.

sentences.zh: 紹逆公孫瓚於界橋，鉅鹿太守李邵及郡冠蓋，以瓚兵強，皆欲屬瓚。

translations.literal: When Shao opposed Gongsun Zan at Jie Bridge, Julu Administrator Li Shao and the county notables, seeing Zan's strength, all wished to attach to Zan.
translations.idiomatic: At Jie Bridge Yuan Shao faced Gongsun Zan; Julu's Li Shao and local gentry, awed by Zan's army, prepared to defect.

sentences.zh: 紹聞之，使昭領鉅鹿。

translations.literal: When Shao heard of it he ordered Zhao to take charge of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent Zhao to govern Julu.

sentences.zh: 問：「御以何術？

translations.literal: He asked: "With what method will you govern them?
translations.idiomatic: Shao asked what tactic he would use.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「一人之微，不能消眾謀，欲誘致其心，唱與同議，及得其情，乃當權以制之耳。

translations.literal: "He replied: "One man's slight weight cannot dissolve many plots; I wish to draw out their hearts, sing the same tune in council, and once I grasp their intent then wield expedients to control them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao answered: "I cannot outweigh a mob single-handed; I will join their chorus until I read their hearts, then seize the moment to master them.

sentences.zh: 計在臨時，未可得言。

translations.literal: The exact stratagem depends on the moment and cannot be stated in advance.
translations.idiomatic: The ruse must wait on events—I cannot spell it out yet.

sentences.zh: 」時郡右姓孫伉等數十人專為謀主，驚動吏民。

translations.literal: "At that time several dozen powerful local lineages such as Sun Kang acted as secret directors of the plot, alarming clerks and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile dozens of magnates including Sun Kang steered the conspiracy and spread panic.

sentences.zh: 昭至郡，偽作紹檄告郡云：「得賊羅候安平張吉辭，當攻鉅鹿，賊故孝廉孫伉等為應，檄到收行軍法，惡止其身，妻子勿坐。

translations.literal: When Zhao reached the commandery he forged Shao's order proclaiming to the county: "Captured testimony from the bandit scout Luo Hou of Anping, Zhang Ji, states an attack on Julu is planned; former Filial and Incorrupt Sun Kang and others are accomplices; upon receipt of this order execute them by military law—punish only their persons, not wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao arrived with a forged edict: confessions from the bandit courier Zhang Ji of Anping implicated Sun Kang's circle in a strike on Julu—when the notice landed, military justice should fall on the plotters alone, sparing families.

sentences.zh: 」昭案檄告令，皆即斬之。

translations.literal: "Zhao displayed the order's commands and immediately beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: He published the forgery and cut down every name on it.

sentences.zh: 一郡惶恐，乃以次安慰，遂皆平集。

translations.literal: The whole commandery trembled with fear; he then comforted them in due order and all settled.
translations.idiomatic: Terror gripped the district until Zhao soothed rank after rank and calm returned.

sentences.zh: 事訖白紹，紹稱善。

translations.literal: When the affair concluded he reported to Shao, who praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao heard the report and approved.

sentences.zh: 會魏郡太守栗攀為兵所害，紹以昭領魏郡太守。

translations.literal: It happened that Wei Commandery Administrator Li Pan fell to mutinous troops and Shao appointed Zhao acting Wei Commandery Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Pan of Wei died to rebels Shao named Zhao to the post.

sentences.zh: 時郡界大亂，賊以萬數，遣使往來，交易市買。

translations.literal: The commandery borders were in great turmoil and bandits numbered in the tens of thousands, sending envoys back and forth to trade in the markets.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits in uncounted thousands infested the frontier, shuttling agents to barter in the towns.

sentences.zh: 昭厚待之，因用為間，乘虛掩討，輒大克破。

translations.literal: Zhao treated them generously and used them as spies; exploiting gaps he struck and consistently won crushing victories.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao feasted their messengers, turned them into informants, and hit empty camps for rout after rout.

sentences.zh: 二日之中，羽檄三至。

translations.literal: Within two days feathered dispatches arrived thrice.
translations.idiomatic: In two days three urgent orders flew in.

sentences.zh: 昭弟訪，在張邈軍中。

translations.literal: Zhao's younger brother Fang was in Zhang Miao's army.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Fang served under Zhang Miao.

sentences.zh: 邈與紹有隙，紹受讒將致罪於昭。

translations.literal: Miao and Shao had quarreled; Shao accepted slander and meant to visit punishment on Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Miao feuded with Shao; poisoned counsel convinced Shao to blame Zhao.

sentences.zh: 昭欲詣漢獻帝，至河內，為張楊所留。

translations.literal: Zhao wished to reach Emperor Xian but at Hanoi was detained by Zhang Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao aimed for the emperor yet Zhang Yang held him at Hanoi.

sentences.zh: 因楊上還印綬，拜騎都尉。

translations.literal: Through Yang he returned his seals and cords and was appointed Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Yang forwarded his resignation of insignia and secured him the post of Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 時太祖領兗州，遣使詣楊，欲令假塗西至長安，楊不聽。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Progenitor held Yan Province and sent envoys to Yang seeking passage west to Chang'an; Yang refused.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao governed Yan and asked Yang for a corridor to Chang'an; Yang declined.

sentences.zh: 昭說楊曰：「袁、曹雖為一家，勢不久羣。

translations.literal: Zhao urged Yang: "Yuan and Cao may seem one house yet their alliance cannot endure.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao told Yang: "Yuan and Cao walk together now but will split.

sentences.zh: 曹今雖弱，然實天下之英雄也，當故結之。

translations.literal: Though Cao is weak today he is in truth a hero of the age—you ought to bind yourself to him by past kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Cao looks feeble yet he is the age's champion—old ties say you should clasp his hand.

sentences.zh: 況今有緣，宜通其上事，並表薦之；

translations.literal: Moreover opportunity now exists: you should relay his memorials upward and jointly recommend him;
translations.idiomatic: The moment favors action—carry his petitions to court and sponsor him;

sentences.zh: 若事有成，永為深分。

translations.literal: if matters succeed you will share a bond forever deep.
translations.idiomatic: success will cement an alliance no shallow tie can match.

sentences.zh: 」楊於是通太祖上事，表薦太祖。

translations.literal: "Yang then forwarded the Grand Progenitor's reports and memorialized to recommend him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang relayed Cao Cao's paperwork and recommended him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 昭為太祖作書與長安諸將李傕、郭汜等，各隨輕重致殷勤。

translations.literal: Zhao drafted letters for the Grand Progenitor to Chang'an generals Li Jue and Guo Si, tailoring warmth to each man's weight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao penned letters for Li Jue, Guo Si, and the western officers—tone matched each man's stature.

sentences.zh: 楊亦遣使詣太祖。

translations.literal: Yang likewise dispatched envoys to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Yang sent his own embassy to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 太祖遺楊犬馬金帛，遂與西方往來。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor sent Yang dogs, horses, gold, and silk, and thereafter traffic opened with the west.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao answered with hounds, horses, gold, and silk—western correspondence flowed.

sentences.zh: 天子在安邑，昭從河內往，詔拜議郎。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven was at Anyi Zhao went from Hanoi and was ordered Gentleman Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: The court sat at Anyi; Zhao traveled from Hanoi and received appointment as Gentleman Consultant.

sentences.zh: 建安元年，太祖定黃巾於許，遣使詣河東。

translations.literal: In Jian'an year one the Grand Progenitor pacified the Yellow Turbans at Xu and sent envoys to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Jian'an year Cao Cao crushed the Turbans at Xu and reached east toward Hedong.

sentences.zh: 會天子還洛陽，韓暹、楊奉、董承及楊各違戾不和。

translations.literal: It happened that the Son of Heaven returned to Luoyang while Han Xian, Yang Feng, Dong Cheng, and Yang each defied the others and quarreled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode back to Luoyang as Han Xian, Yang Feng, Dong Cheng, and Zhang Yang feuded.

sentences.zh: 昭以奉兵馬最強而少黨援，作太祖書與奉曰：

translations.literal: Because Feng's troops were strongest yet lacked allies Zhao forged a letter from the Grand Progenitor to Feng saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yang Feng commanded the strongest horse but no friends; Zhao drafted Cao Cao's voice to him:

sentences.zh: 吾與將軍聞名慕義，便推赤心。

translations.literal: You and I, General, have heard each other's names and admired righteousness—let us lay bare our hearts.
translations.idiomatic: General, we have long esteemed each other from afar—let our loyalty show.

sentences.zh: 今將軍拔萬乘之艱難，反之舊都，翼佐之功，超世無疇，何其休哉！

translations.literal: Now you have wrested the sovereign through hardship and restored the old capital—such auxiliary merit exceeds any parallel age can offer; how splendid!
translations.idiomatic: You dragged the throne through fire back to Luoyang—no aide of any era matches that glory.

sentences.zh: 方今羣凶猾夏，四海未寧，神器至重，事在維輔；

translations.literal: Today vicious factions ravage the Xia lands; the four seas are unquiet and the divine regalia weigh utmost—the task lies in sustaining pillars;
translations.idiomatic: Rebels still scour China; the realm trembles and the imperial tokens demand guardians—

sentences.zh: 必須眾賢以清王軌，誠非一人所能獨建。

translations.literal: many worthy men must cleanse the king's tracks; truly no single man can erect this alone.
translations.idiomatic: a bench of sages must scrub the royal road—no lone arm suffices.

sentences.zh: 心腹四支，實相恃賴，一物不備，則有闕焉。

translations.literal: Heart and four limbs truly rely on one another—lack one member and the body fails.
translations.idiomatic: Trunk and limbs need each other—lose one piece and the frame collapses.

sentences.zh: 將軍當為內主，吾為外援。

translations.literal: You should serve as inner pillar while I act as outer shield.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the capital's core; I shield from without.

sentences.zh: 今吾有糧，將軍有兵，有無相通，足以相濟，死生契闊，相與共之。

translations.literal: Now I have grain and you have arms; sharing surplus and want we can sustain each other—in life or death, separation or reunion, we walk together.
translations.idiomatic: My granaries pair with your spears—swap plenty for need and neither starves; swear through fortune and ruin alike.

sentences.zh: 奉得書喜悅，語諸將軍曰：「兗州諸軍近在許耳，有兵有糧，國家所當依仰也。

translations.literal: When Feng received the letter he rejoiced and told his generals: "The Yan Province army camps near Xu with troops and grain—the state must lean upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Feng read the note with delight: "Cao Cao's Yan corps hug Xu with men and stores—the court should cling to him.

sentences.zh: 」遂共表太祖為鎮東將軍，襲父爵費亭侯；

translations.literal: "Together they memorialized the Grand Progenitor as General Who Guards the East and let him inherit his father's village marquisate of Feiting;
translations.idiomatic: Jointly they proposed Cao Cao as General Who Guards the East and heir to the Feiting fief;

sentences.zh: 昭遷符節令。

translations.literal: Zhao was promoted Bearer of the Tallies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao rose to Bearer of Tallies and Seals.

sentences.zh: 太祖朝天子於洛陽，引昭並坐，問曰：「今孤來此，當施何計？

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor attended the Son of Heaven at Luoyang he seated Zhao beside him and asked: "Now that I have come what plan should I pursue?
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang audience Cao Cao drew Zhao to his side: "What move comes next?

sentences.zh: 」昭曰：「將軍興義兵以誅暴亂，入朝天子，輔翼王室，此五伯之功也。

translations.literal: "Zhao replied: "You raised righteous troops to punish violence, entered court to attend the Son of Heaven, and shore the royal house—work worthy of the Five Hegemons.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao answered: "You marched under righteous banners, entered to serve the emperor, and brace the dynasty—hegemon-grade service.

sentences.zh: 此下諸將，人殊意異，未必服從，今留匡弼，事勢不便，惟有移駕幸許耳。

translations.literal: The generals below each harbor divergent intent and may not obey; to remain merely correcting matters grows awkward—only removing the court to Xu will serve.
translations.idiomatic: Your colonels nurse private schemes—staying to "assist" courts awkwardness; shifting the throne to Xu is the lever.

sentences.zh: 然朝廷播越，新還舊京，遠近跂望，冀一朝獲安。

translations.literal: Yet the court has wandered and newly returned to the old capital; far and near crane their necks hoping one morning brings peace.
translations.idiomatic: The throne just limped home to Luoyang and every county watches for stability.

sentences.zh: 今復徙駕，不厭眾心。

translations.literal: To move the chariot again will dissatisfy popular expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Another relocation strains patience.

sentences.zh: 夫行非常之事，乃有非常之功，原將軍算其多者。

translations.literal: Yet extraordinary deeds yield extraordinary merit—I beg you weigh the greater gain.
translations.idiomatic: Still, bold strokes earn bold renown—weigh the larger arithmetic.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「此孤本志也。

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor said: "That has always been my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said: "That was always my aim.

sentences.zh: 楊奉近在梁耳，聞其兵精，得無為孤累乎？

translations.literal: Yang Feng camps near Liang with elite troops—might he burden me?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Feng sits near Liang with veteran horse—will he block us?

sentences.zh: 」昭曰：「奉少黨援，將獨委質。

translations.literal: "Zhao said: "Feng lacks allies and will cast his lot alone.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao replied: "Feng stands alone and must swear fealty.

sentences.zh: 鎮東、費亭之事，皆奉所定，又聞書命申束，足以見信。

translations.literal: The appointments as Guard East and Feiting marquis were settled through him and his letters bind him—enough to prove trust.
translations.idiomatic: He brokered your eastern command and Feiting title—his correspondence already binds him.

sentences.zh: 宜時遣使厚遺答謝，以安其意。

translations.literal: Send envoys at once with rich gifts in thanks to steady his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch messengers laden with gifts to soothe him.

sentences.zh: 說『京都無糧，欲車駕暫幸魯陽，魯陽近許，轉運稍易，可無縣乏之憂』。

translations.literal: Explain that 'the capital lacks grain and wishes to move the court temporarily to Luyang—Luyang lies close to Xu so transport eases and supplies need not fail counties.
translations.idiomatic: Explain the capital starves and seeks interim quarters at Luyang—near Xu for easier convoys.

sentences.zh: 奉為人勇而寡慮，必不見疑，比使往來，足以定計。

translations.literal: Feng is brave yet shallow-thinking—he will not suspect; repeated embassies will fix the strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Feng values daring over reflection—he will swallow the tale; shuttling envoys seals the plan.

sentences.zh: 奉何能為累！

translations.literal: How could Feng become a burden!
translations.idiomatic: Feng poses no real obstacle.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「善。

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor said: "Excellent.
translations.idiomatic: "Good," said Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 」即遣使詣奉。

translations.literal: "He immediately sent envoys to Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys rode to Feng.

sentences.zh: 徙大駕至許。

translations.literal: The great chariot shifted to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relocated to Xu.

sentences.zh: 奉由是失望，與韓暹等到定陵鈔暴。

translations.literal: Thereupon Feng was disappointed and with Han Xian and others reached Dingling to pillage.
translations.idiomatic: Feng, bitter, joined Han Xian raiding toward Dingling.

sentences.zh: 太祖不應，密往攻其梁營，降誅即定。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor did not answer openly but secretly marched to storm his Liang camp, accepting surrender and executing leaders until order stood.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao feigned indifference then struck Feng's Liang camp by night—surrender and beheadings settled it.

sentences.zh: 奉、暹失眾，東降袁術。

translations.literal: Feng and Xian lost their hosts and went east to surrender to Yuan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of followers they fled east to Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 三年，昭遷河南尹。

translations.literal: In the third year Zhao was transferred Administrator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Third Jian'an year brought Zhao the Henan administrator's seal.

sentences.zh: 時張楊為其將楊醜所殺，楊長史薛洪、河內太守繆尚城守待紹救。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yang was killed by his officer Yang Chou; Yang's chief clerk Xue Hong and Hanoi Administrator Miao Shang held the city awaiting Shao's rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chou murdered Zhang Yang; Xue Hong and Miao Shang walled Hanoi for Yuan Shao relief.

sentences.zh: 太祖令昭單身入城，告喻洪、尚等，即日舉眾降。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor ordered Zhao to enter the city alone and persuade Hong and Shang; that same day they led the multitude to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Zhao unescorted through the gates; Hong and Shang capitulated the same hour.

sentences.zh: 以昭為冀州牧。

translations.literal: Zhao was appointed Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Province went to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 太祖令劉備拒袁術，昭曰：「備勇而志大，關羽、張飛為之羽翼，恐備之心未可得論也！

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor ordered Liu Bei to block Yuan Shu Zhao said: "Bei is bold and ambitious with Guan Yu and Zhang Fei as wings—you cannot fathom his heart!
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao tasked Liu Bei against Shu, Zhao warned: "Bei dreams large with Guan and Zhang as talons—his loyalty is unreadable!

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「吾已許之矣。

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor said: "I have already promised.
translations.idiomatic: "I gave my word," Cao Cao answered.

sentences.zh: 」備到下邳，殺徐州刺史車冑，反。

translations.literal: "When Bei reached Xiapi he killed Xu Province Inspector Che Zhou and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Bei rode to Xiapi, slew Che Zhou, and revolted.

sentences.zh: 太祖自征備，徙昭為徐州牧。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor personally campaigned against Bei and transferred Zhao to Governor of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao marched in person and moved Zhao to Xu governor.

sentences.zh: 袁紹遣將顏良攻東郡，又徙昭為魏郡太守，從討良。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao sent general Yan Liang against Dong Commandery; Zhao was shifted to Wei Commandery Administrator and joined the punitive expedition against Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Shao hurled Yan Liang at Dongjun; Zhao became Wei administrator and joined the strike.

sentences.zh: 良死後，進圍鄴城。

translations.literal: After Liang died they advanced to besiege Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liang fell the army ringed Ye.

sentences.zh: 袁紹同族春卿為魏郡太守，在城中，其父元長在揚州，太祖遣人迎之。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao's clansman Chunqing served as Wei Commandery Administrator inside the city while his father Yuan Chang was in Yang Province; the Grand Progenitor sent men to welcome Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chunqing held Wei from within while his father Yuan Chang tarried in the south; Cao Cao fetched the elder.

sentences.zh: 昭書與春卿曰：

translations.literal: Zhao wrote Chunqing saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's letter to Chunqing read:

sentences.zh: 蓋聞孝者不背親以要利，仁者不忘君以徇私，志士不探亂以徼幸，智者不詭道以自危。

translations.literal: I have heard that the filial do not abandon kin for profit, the humane do not forget their lord for private gain, high-minded men do not probe chaos for luck, and the wise do not twist the Way to court peril.
translations.idiomatic: They say the dutiful never sell parents for gain, the humane never shelve their prince for selfish ends, the resolute never mine turmoil for fortune, and the wise never bend principle toward ruin.

sentences.zh: 足下大君，昔避內難，南游百越，非疏骨肉，樂彼吳會，智者深識，獨或宜然。

translations.literal: Your noble father once fled domestic strife and roamed the southern Yue—not from spurning flesh and blood nor loving Wu and Kuaiji, but because far-sighted judgment sometimes demands it.
translations.idiomatic: Your father fled civil war into the far south—not because he scorned kin or adored Wu, but because foresight sometimes demands retreat.

sentences.zh: 曹公愍其守志清恪，離羣寡儔，故特遣使江東，或迎或送，今將至矣。

translations.literal: Lord Cao pities his steadfast purity and lonely exile and therefore specially dispatched envoys along the Yangzi either to escort or receive—he nears arrival now.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao admires his integrity in exile and sends boats east to bring him—expect him soon.

sentences.zh: 就令足下處偏平之地，依德義之主，居有泰山之固，身為喬松之偶，以義言之，猶宜背彼向此，舍民趣父也。

translations.literal: Suppose you stood on level ground under a lord of virtue with Mount Tai for ramparts and pine companions for company—even then duty says turn from them toward this, leave the crowd and hurry to your father.
translations.idiomatic: Even had you safe walls under a sage king, righteousness still bids you quit posts for your father's arms.

sentences.zh: 且邾儀父始與隱公盟，魯​​人嘉之，而不書爵，然則王所未命，爵尊不成，春秋之義也。

translations.literal: Moreover when Yi Fu of Zhu first covenanted with Duke Yin the people of Lu praised him yet recorded no rank—thus without royal investiture exalted title cannot stand; such is Spring and Autumn principle.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu's Yi Fu swore with Duke Yin, Lu praised him yet withheld noble rank—without the king's patent rank cannot hold; that is Annals teaching.

sentences.zh: 況足下今日之所託者乃危亂之國，所受者乃矯誣之命乎？

translations.literal: How much more when today's refuge is a realm in peril and your commission a forged pretense?
translations.idiomatic: Worse still you cling to a doomed court under counterfeit orders.

sentences.zh: 苟不逞之與羣，而厥父之不恤，不可以言孝。

translations.literal: If you herd with the unruly yet spare no thought for the father who sired you, one cannot call it filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Plotting with rebels while ignoring the father who raised you is not filial.

sentences.zh: 忘祖宗所居之本朝，安非正之姦職，難可以言忠。

translations.literal: To forget the dynastic house where your ancestors dwelt and cling to an irregular traitor's office—can that be called loyalty?
translations.idiomatic: Forgetting the legitimate court your clan served to serve usurpers is not loyalty.

sentences.zh: 忠孝並替，難以言智。

translations.literal: With loyalty and filial piety both forfeited how can one speak of wisdom?
translations.idiomatic: Lose both virtues and wisdom vanishes.

sentences.zh: 又足下昔日為曹公所禮辟，夫戚族人而疏所生，內所寓而外王室，懷邪祿而叛知己，遠福祚而近危亡，棄明義而收大恥，不亦可惜邪！

translations.literal: Moreover you once answered Lord Cao's summons with honor—to slight blood kin for distant connections, lodge inwardly with rebels yet outwardly wear royal colors, cherish wicked stipends while betraying the man who knew you, chase peril instead of fortune, embrace shame instead of bright principle—is that not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: You accepted Cao Cao's respectful call yet now favor strangers over parents, mouth loyalty while aiding rebels, fatten on treacherous salary and spurn your patron—trading blessing for ruin and honor for infamy!

sentences.zh: 若能翻然易節，奉帝養父，委身曹公，忠孝不墜，榮名彰矣。

translations.literal: If you can reverse course overnight, serve the emperor and shelter your father, and devote yourself to Lord Cao, loyalty and filial duty remain intact and glorious fame shines.
translations.idiomatic: Turn now: obey the throne, rescue your father, bind yourself to Cao Cao—duty stays whole and renown gleams.

sentences.zh: 宜深留計，早決良圖。

translations.literal: Deliberate deeply and settle a worthy plan early.
translations.idiomatic: Think hard and choose quickly.

sentences.zh: 鄴既定，以昭為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: After Ye submitted Zhao was appointed Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's fall made Zhao Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 後袁尚依烏丸蹋頓，太祖將征之。

translations.literal: Later when Yuan Shang sheltered with Wuhuan chieftain Tadun the Grand Progenitor prepared to campaign;
translations.idiomatic: When Shang fled to Tadun Cao Cao eyed the north;

sentences.zh: 患軍糧難致，鑿平虜、泉州二渠入海通運，昭所建也。

translations.literal: worrying grain supply would not reach the army he dug the Pinglu and Quanzhou canals to the sea for transport—Zhao's design.
translations.idiomatic: anxious over logistics Zhao cut the Pinglu and Quanzhou canals to feed supply ships.

sentences.zh: 太祖表封千秋亭侯，轉拜司空軍祭酒。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor memorialized enfeoffment as village marquis of Qianqiu and transferred him Libationer of the Army under the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao enfeoffed him village marquis of Qianqiu and named him army libationer.

sentences.zh: 後昭建議：「宜脩古建封五等。

translations.literal: Later Zhao proposed: "It is fitting to restore antiquity and establish the five ranks of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao urged reviving the classical five-grade enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「建設五等者，聖人也，又非人臣所製，吾何以堪之？

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor said: "Founding the five ranks belongs to sages; further it is not for ministers to devise—how could I bear it?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao answered: "Only sages erect those ranks; ministers may not invent them—how dare I?

sentences.zh: 」昭曰：

translations.literal: "Zhao said:
translations.idiomatic: Zhao replied:

sentences.zh: 自古以來，人臣匡世，未有今日之功。

translations.literal: Since antiquity no minister who steadied the age has matched today's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: No servant who righted the realm ever matched your ledger.

sentences.zh: 有今日之功，未有久處人臣之勢者也。

translations.literal: With today's achievement none has long remained merely a minister's posture.
translations.idiomatic: No one who scaled such heights stayed forever the subject's stance.

sentences.zh: 今明公恥有慚德而未盡善，樂保名節而無大責，德美過於伊、周，此至德之所極也。

translations.literal: Now my enlightened lord blushes at imperfect virtue yet guards reputation without grave blame—your moral beauty surpasses Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou; this is the utmost of perfect virtue.
translations.idiomatic: You fret over moral blemish yet keep unstained name—your excellence outshines Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, the summit of sage conduct.

sentences.zh: 然太甲、成王未必可遭，今民難化，甚於殷、周，處大臣之勢，使人以大事疑己，誠不可不重慮也。

translations.literal: Yet rulers like Taijia or King Cheng may not appear again; the people now resist transformation more than Yin or Zhou subjects; standing as great minister while others suspect you of grand designs—ponder that with utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: Taijia's redemption or Cheng's youth may never recur; commoners today prove harder to mold than Shang or Zhou peasants; wielding supreme ministerial power while the world eyes you for higher ambition demands cold reckoning.

sentences.zh: 明公雖邁威德，明法術，而不定其基，為萬世計，猶未至也。

translations.literal: Though my enlightened lord surpasses others in awe-inspiring virtue and clarifies laws and methods, without fixing his foundations or planning for posterity he has not yet reached completeness.
translations.idiomatic: You tower in prestige and statute, yet until you secure your base for generations to come the edifice stays unfinished.

sentences.zh: 定基之本，在地與人，宜稍建立，以自籓衛。

translations.literal: The root of fixing foundations lies in land and men; you should gradually erect supports to fence and guard yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Lay foundations in territory and talent—build bulwarks step by step so you can shield what you hold.

sentences.zh: 明公忠節穎露，天威在顏，耿弇床下之言，硃英無妄之論，不得過耳。

translations.literal: Your lordship's loyal integrity shines conspicuously and heavenly majesty rests on your brow—counsel like Geng Yan's bedside words or Zhu Ying's warning against rash deeds cannot pass unheard.
translations.idiomatic: Your name for loyalty blazes and imperial gravity sits on your brow—no whisper rivals Geng Yan's midnight plea or Zhu Ying's sober caution.

sentences.zh: 昭受恩非凡，不敢不陳。

translations.literal: Zhao received extraordinary favor and dared not withhold statement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao owed rare kindness and could not stay silent.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝春秋》曰：昭與列侯諸將議，以丞相宜進爵國公，九錫備物，以彰殊勳；

translations.literal: 《Annals of Emperor Xian》 records: Zhao debated with ranked nobles and generals that the Chancellor ought to advance to Duke of State with the nine ritual gifts complete to honor singular merit;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xian's chronicle notes Zhao urging the court to raise the Chancellor to duke rank with full nine bestowals for unmatched service;

sentences.zh: 書與荀彧曰：「昔周旦、呂望，當姬氏之盛，因二聖之業，輔翼成王之幼，功勳若彼，猶受上爵，錫土開宇。

translations.literal: He wrote Xun Yu: "Formerly Duke of Zhou and Lü Wang, amid the Ji clan's flourishing, building on the two sages' enterprise, aided the young King Cheng—with merit such as theirs they still received supreme noble rank and grants of land opening territory.
translations.idiomatic: His letter to Xun Yu recalled how the Duke of Zhou and Taigong Wang, at Zhou's zenith, steadied boy-king Cheng yet still earned top titles and broad fiefs.

sentences.zh: 末世田單，驅強齊之眾，報弱燕之怨，收城七十，迎复襄王；

translations.literal: At a dynasty's end Tian Dan drove mighty Qi's masses to avenge weak Yan, recovered seventy cities and welcomed King Xiang back;
translations.idiomatic: Late in an age Tian Dan mobilized mighty Qi to humble Yan, retook seventy towns, and restored King Xiang;

sentences.zh: 襄王加賞於單，使東有掖邑之封，西有菑上之虞。

translations.literal: King Xiang layered rewards on Dan, granting Ye settlement east and Zi uplands west.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang heaped honors on Dan—Ye east of the river, Zi heights west.

sentences.zh: 前世錄功，濃厚如此。

translations.literal: Earlier ages recorded merit so generously.
translations.idiomatic: Past courts weighed merit this lavishly.

sentences.zh: 今曹公遭海內傾覆，宗廟焚滅，躬擐甲胄，周旋征伐，櫛風沐雨，且三十年，芟夷羣凶，為百姓除害，使漢室復存，劉氏奉祀。

translations.literal: Now Lord Cao has suffered the realm overturned and ancestral temples burned; personally donning armor he has campaigned thirty years through wind and rain, extirpating villains, removing harm for the common people, restoring the Han house and Liu ancestral sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Cao faced empire-wide ruin and burnt shrines; thirty years in harness through storm he swept predators aside, saved the people, revived Han, and kept Liu offerings alive.

sentences.zh: 方之曩者數公，若太山之與丘垤，豈同日而論乎？

translations.literal: Compared to those former men it is Mount Tai beside a molehill—how speak of them on the same day?
translations.idiomatic: Set him beside those ancients and it is Taishan beside a molehill—no honest comparison exists.

sentences.zh: 今徒與列將功臣，並侯一縣，此豈天下所望哉！」〉

translations.literal: Now he merely shares county-level marquisates with ranking generals and merit holders—is this what the realm expects!"〉
translations.idiomatic: Yet today he splits county marquessates with captains—is that what the world hoped for?"

sentences.zh: 後太祖遂受魏公、魏王之號，皆昭所創。

translations.literal: Later the Grand Progenitor accepted the titles Duke of Wei and King of Wei—all Zhao's initiative.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao later took Duke and King of Wei—every step traced to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 及關羽圍曹仁於樊，孫權遣使辭以「遣兵西上，欲掩取羽。

translations.literal: When Guan Yu besieged Cao Ren at Fan, Sun Quan sent envoys saying he would "dispatch troops west intending to strike Guan Yu by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: At Fan Guan Yu penned Cao Ren while Sun Quan pledged to march west and ambush Yu;

sentences.zh: 江陵、公安累重，羽失二城，必自奔走，樊軍之圍，不救自解。

translations.literal: Jiangling and Gong'an are heavily fortified; should Yu lose both cities he will surely flee on his own and the Fan siege will loosen without rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Lose Jiangling and Gong'an and Yu bolts—the Fan cordon slackens untouched.

sentences.zh: 乞密不漏，令羽有備。

translations.literal: Beg secrecy lest Yu gain warning.
translations.idiomatic: Keep it dark so Yu stays blind.

sentences.zh: 」太祖詰羣臣，羣臣咸言宜當密之。

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor questioned his ministers; all said it ought to be kept secret.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao polled his council; every voice favored concealment.

sentences.zh: 昭曰：「軍事尚權，期於合宜。

translations.literal: Zhao said: "Military affairs esteem expedience—the aim is fitness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao answered: "War prizes timing—fitness beats dogma.

sentences.zh: 宜應權以密，而內露之。

translations.literal: Outwardly one should answer with secrecy yet inwardly leak it.
translations.idiomatic: Promise silence abroad while leaking truth within.

sentences.zh: 羽聞權上，若還自護，圍則速解，便獲其利。

translations.literal: When Yu hears Quan has gone upstream he may return to guard himself—the siege then quickly dissolves and we gain advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Yu learns Sun Quan sails west and wheels home—Fan lifts fast while we profit.

sentences.zh: 可使兩賊相對銜持，坐待其弊。

translations.literal: We can set the two bandits snarling at each other and sit awaiting their exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Let the two predators leash each other while we watch them tire.

sentences.zh: 秘而不露，使權得志，非計之上。

translations.literal: To hide it utterly and let Quan have his way is not top strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Total secrecy hands Sun Quan free rein—that is second-rate craft.

sentences.zh: 又，圍中將吏不知有救，計糧怖懼，儻有他意，為難不小。

translations.literal: Moreover officers inside the siege know not of rescue; calculating grain they panic—with other intentions stirred trouble would be no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged men hear no relief and count dwindling grain—panic breeds mutiny if unchecked.

sentences.zh: 露之為便。

translations.literal: Leaking is advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Leak the news.

sentences.zh: 且羽為人強梁，自恃二城守固，必不速退。

translations.literal: Moreover Yu is obstinate and trusts the two cities' defenses firm—he will not retreat quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Yu is stubborn and trusts his twin bastions—he will not slip away soon.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「善。

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor said: "Excellent.
translations.idiomatic: "Good," said Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 」即敕救將徐晃以權書射著圍裡及羽屯中，圍裡聞之，志氣百倍。

translations.literal: "He immediately ordered relief general Xu Huang to shoot Sun Quan's letter into the siege ring and Guan Yu's camp; hearing it morale inside multiplied a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: He told Xu Huang to loft Sun Quan's dispatch into Fan and Yu's lines—defenders roared with fresh heart.

sentences.zh: 羽果猶豫。

translations.literal: Yu indeed hesitated.
translations.idiomatic: Yu stalled, torn.

sentences.zh: 權軍至，得其二城，羽乃破敗。

translations.literal: When Quan's army arrived and took both cities Yu was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan seized two towns and broke Yu.

sentences.zh: 文帝即王位，拜昭將作大匠。

translations.literal: When the Wen Emperor assumed kingship he appointed Zhao Grand Engineer.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi as king named Zhao Chief of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，遷大鴻臚，進封右鄉侯。

translations.literal: Upon ascending he promoted him Grand Herald and advanced the fief to village marquis of Youxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On the throne he raised Zhao to Grand Herald and village marquis of Youxiang.

sentences.zh: 二年，分邑百戶，賜昭弟訪爵關內侯，徙昭為侍中。

translations.literal: Second year he divided out one hundred households and enfeoffed Zhao's younger brother Fang as secondary marquis within the passes; Zhao was transferred Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Year two brought Fang a hundred-household noble stipend inside the passes while Zhao moved to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 三年，征東大將軍曹休臨江在洞浦口，自表：「原將銳卒虎步江南，因敵取資，事必克捷；

translations.literal: Third year General Who Conquers the East Cao Xiu faced the river at Dongpu inlet and memorialized: "I wish to lead crack troops tiger-stepping south of the Yangzi, feeding off the enemy—the deed must succeed;
translations.idiomatic: Year three saw Cao Xiu at Dongpu petitioning to drive elite columns across Wu and live off hostile granaries;

sentences.zh: 若其無臣，不須為念。

translations.literal: Should plans miscarry Your Majesty need not fret.
translations.idiomatic: If fortune fails, lose no sleep over it.

sentences.zh: 」帝恐休便渡江，驛馬詔止。

translations.literal: "The Emperor feared Xiu might cross at once and dispatched relay horses with edict to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a rash ford Cao Pi raced counterorders.

sentences.zh: 時昭侍側，因曰：「竊見陛下有憂色，獨以休濟江故乎？

translations.literal: Zhao attending said: "Your servant spies worry on Your Majesty's brow—is it solely Xiu crossing the river?
translations.idiomatic: At audience Zhao whispered: "Your face clouds—is it Xiu fording the Yangzi?

sentences.zh: 今者渡江，人情所難，就休有此志，勢不獨行，當須諸將。

translations.literal: Crossing now is what men dread; even had Xiu such intent he could not go alone—he needs the generals.
translations.idiomatic: A river crossing unnerves every soldier; Xiu cannot swim it solo—colonels must follow.

sentences.zh: 臧霸等既富且貴，無復他望，但欲終其天年，保守祿祚而已，何肯乘危自投死地，以求徼倖？

translations.literal: Zang Ba and others are already wealthy and titled, cherish no further ambition, only wish to finish their natural span guarding stipends—why would they ride peril into death seeking luck?
translations.idiomatic: Zang Ba and peers already feast on rank—they seek quiet pensions, not dice-with-death gambles.

sentences.zh: 苟霸等不進，休意自沮。

translations.literal: If Ba and others do not advance Xiu's intent collapses of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Hold Ba back and Xiu's urge dies.

sentences.zh: 臣恐陛下雖有敕渡之詔，猶必沉吟，未便從命也。

translations.literal: Your servant fears though Your Majesty issued edict permitting crossing they will still hesitate and not obey at once.
translations.idiomatic: Even green-light edicts may leave generals dragging their feet.

sentences.zh: 」是後無幾，暴風吹賊船，悉詣休等營下，斬首獲生，賊遂迸散。

translations.literal: "Shortly after a gale drove enemy ships all under Xiu's camp—heads taken captives seized—and the bandits scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a squall washed Wu hulls under Xiu's guns—heads piled, prisoners flooded—foes melted.

sentences.zh: 詔敕諸軍促渡。

translations.literal: Edict urged all armies to hurry the crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh orders pressed every column to ford.

sentences.zh: 軍未時進，賊救船遂至。

translations.literal: Troops had not advanced in time when enemy rescue ships arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Before lines crossed Wu relief hulls closed.

sentences.zh: 大駕幸宛，征南大將軍夏侯尚等攻江陵，未拔。

translations.literal: The imperial train visited Wan; General Who Conquers the South Xiahou Shang besieged Jiangling without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: The court moved to Wan while Xiahou Shang hammered Jiangling in vain.

sentences.zh: 時江水淺狹，尚欲乘船將步騎入渚中安屯，作浮橋，南北往來，議者多以為城必可拔。

translations.literal: The river ran shallow and narrow; Shang wished to ferry infantry and cavalry aboard boats into mid-channel islets to camp, building floating bridges for north-south passage—most debaters thought the city sure to fall.
translations.idiomatic: Low water tempted Shang to island-hop horse and foot, spanpon bridges north and south—counselors assumed the town must yield.

sentences.zh: 昭上疏曰：

translations.literal: Zhao submitted memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhao memorialized:

sentences.zh: 武皇帝智勇過人，而用兵畏敵，不敢輕之若此也。

translations.literal: Martial Emperor surpassed men in wit and courage yet feared the enemy in deploying troops—never lightly thus.
translations.idiomatic: Martial Emperor owned genius and nerve yet treated foes with dread—never rash.

sentences.zh: 夫兵好進惡退，常然之數。

translations.literal: Troops love advance and hate retreat—that is constant tendency.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers crave attack and dread withdrawal—that law holds.

sentences.zh: 平地無險，猶尚艱難，就當深入，還道宜利，兵有進退，不可如意。

translations.literal: Level ground without obstacles is still hard; suppose deep penetration—the return route ought favor withdrawal; troops advance and retreat as circumstance allows—not always as wished.
translations.idiomatic: Open plains still punish armies; drive deep and exits narrow—movement follows fate, not whim.

sentences.zh: 今屯渚中，至深也；

translations.literal: Now camping mid-channel is deepest penetration;
translations.idiomatic: Sandbar camps mean deepest thrust;

sentences.zh: 浮橋而濟，至危也；

translations.literal: floating-bridge crossing is utmost peril;
translations.idiomatic: pontoon crossings spell utmost peril;

sentences.zh: 一道而行，至狹也：三者兵家所忌，而今行之。

translations.literal: single-file march is narrowest passage—these three armies taboo yet now we practice them.
translations.idiomatic: one road binds every rank—three faults strategists shun, yet we embrace them.

sentences.zh: 賊頻攻橋，誤有漏失，渚中精銳，非魏之有，將轉化為吳矣。

translations.literal: If bandits repeatedly assault the bridge and some slip fails the crack troops in the islets cease to be Wei's—they convert to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu hammer the spans once breach opens—Wei elites stranded midstream become Sun trophies.

sentences.zh: 臣私慼之，忘寢與食，而議者怡然不以為憂，豈不惑哉！

translations.literal: Your servant privately grieves, forgetting sleep and food, while debaters remain calm unconcerned—is this not delusion!
translations.idiomatic: Your servant cannot eat or sleep while advisors toast calm—is that sane?

sentences.zh: 加江水向長，一旦暴增，何以防禦？

translations.literal: Moreover the Yangzi rises toward flood season—should it swell overnight how defend?
translations.idiomatic: The great river swells toward summer—who holds a sudden surge?

sentences.zh: 就不破賊，尚當自完。

translations.literal: Grant we fail to break the enemy we still ought preserve ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Fail to storm yet still must save the army.

sentences.zh: 奈何乘危，不以為懼？

translations.literal: Why ride danger without fear?
translations.idiomatic: Why hug peril so casually?

sentences.zh: 事將危矣，惟陛下察之！

translations.literal: Matters verge on peril—only Your Majesty examine them!
translations.idiomatic: Disaster knocks—please weigh it, Majesty!

sentences.zh: 太和四年，行司徒事，六年，拜真。

translations.literal: Fourth year of Taihe he acted Steward's duties; sixth year received full appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe four he handled Steward business; Taihe six he took the seal outright.

sentences.zh: 昭上疏陳末流之弊曰：

translations.literal: Zhao memorialized decrying late-age abuses saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhao warned against decay:

sentences.zh: 凡有天下者，莫不貴尚敦朴忠信之士，深疾虛偽不真之人者，以其毀教亂治，敗俗傷化也。

translations.literal: All who hold the realm honor plain loyal trustworthy men and deeply hate false inauthentic persons—for they ruin teaching, disorder rule, corrupt custom and wound transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Every throne esteems honest servants and loathes fraudsters—they unravel doctrine, wreck government, poison manners.

sentences.zh: 近魏諷則伏誅建安之末，曹偉則斬戮黃初之始。

translations.literal: Recently Wei Feng was executed at Jian'an's end and Cao Wei beheaded at Huang-chu's start.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Feng died late Jian'an; Cao Wei fell early Huangchu.

sentences.zh: 伏惟前後聖詔，深疾浮偽，欲以破散邪黨，常用切齒；

translations.literal: Humbly considering successive sagely edicts deeply hated hollow fraud wishing to smash wicked cliques—often gnashing teeth;
translations.idiomatic: Sacred edicts gnash at glittering deceit and vow to break cabals;

sentences.zh: 而執法之吏皆畏其權勢，莫能糾擿，毀壞風俗，侵欲滋甚。

translations.literal: yet executing officers all feared their power and could not impeach—custom ruined greed spread worse.
translations.idiomatic: yet bailiffs quailed before grandees—custom rotted while greed spread.

sentences.zh: 竊見當今年少，不復以學問為本，專更以交遊為業；

translations.literal: Your servant observes youths today no longer take learning as foundation but exchange visits as occupation;
translations.idiomatic: Youth today trades study for networking;

sentences.zh: 國士不以孝悌清脩為首，乃以趨勢遊利為先。

translations.literal: gentlemen of state rank not filial piety and pure cultivation first but chasing influence and roaming profit ahead.
translations.idiomatic: leading men prize connections over filial purity.

sentences.zh: 合黨連羣，互相褒嘆，以毀訾為罰戮，用黨譽為爵賞，附己者則嘆之盈言，不附者則為作瑕釁。

translations.literal: They gang together praising each other, making slander punishment and clique praise reward—followers win overflowing praise, non-followers suffer manufactured flaws.
translations.idiomatic: Cliques trade flattery for offices—join and earn hymns; refuse and earn fiction.

sentences.zh: 至乃相謂『今世何憂不度邪，但求人道不勤，羅之不博耳；

translations.literal: They even tell each other 'what worry today of not succeeding—only strive insufficiently at cultivating connections, netting too narrow';
translations.idiomatic: They joke that success needs merely wider nets and louder favors;

sentences.zh: 又何患其不知己矣，但當吞之以藥而柔調耳。

translations.literal: 'why fear they won't know us—only dose them with medicine and coax softly.'
translations.idiomatic: they boast secret potions and smooth tongues can sway any patron.

sentences.zh: 』又聞或有使奴客名作在職家人，冒之出入，往來禁奧，交通書疏，有所探問。

translations.literal: Your servant further hears some register slaves and retainers under household names of serving officials to slip in and out of forbidden precincts exchanging letters and probing.
translations.idiomatic: Slaves borrow mandarin names to haunt palace gates, ferrying letters and gossip.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸事，皆法之所不取，刑之所不赦，雖諷、偉之罪，無以加也。

translations.literal: All such acts law forbids and execution must not spare—even Feng and Wei's crimes add nothing worse.
translations.idiomatic: Statute condemns every item—no heavier guilt than Feng or Wei showed.

sentences.zh: 帝於是發切詔，斥免諸葛誕、鄧颺等。

translations.literal: The Emperor then issued stern edict cashiering Zhuge Dan, Deng Yang and others.
translations.idiomatic: The throne answered with biting orders demoting Zhuge Dan, Deng Yang, company.

sentences.zh: 昭年八十一薨，諡曰定侯。

translations.literal: Zhao died at eighty-one; posthumous title Marquis Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He expired at eighty-one as Marquis Ding.

sentences.zh: 子冑嗣。

translations.literal: Son Zhou inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Son Zhou succeeded.

sentences.zh: 冑歷位郡守、九卿。

translations.literal: Zhou successively served commandery governor and nine ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou rose through prefectures to nine ministries.

sentences.zh: 劉曄字子揚，淮南成德人，

translations.literal: Liu Ye, courtesy Ziyang, was a man of Chengde in Huainan,
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ye, style Ziyang, hailed from Chengde in Huainan,

sentences.zh: 〈惪音德。〉

translations.literal: 〈Editorial note: the variant graph is glossed with the reading dé, meaning virtue.〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentarial gloss: read the unusual character as dé (virtue).

sentences.zh: 漢光武子阜陵王延後也。

translations.literal: Descendant of Emperor Guangwu's son Prince Fuling Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He descended from Guangwu's Prince Yan of Fuling.

sentences.zh: 父普，母脩，產渙及曄。

translations.literal: Father Pu, mother Xiu, bore Huan and Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Father Pu and mother Xiu raised brothers Huan and Ye.

sentences.zh: 渙九歲，曄七歲，而母病困。

translations.literal: Huan was nine and Ye seven when their mother fell gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: At nine and seven the boys watched their mother sink.

sentences.zh: 臨終，戒渙、曄以「普之侍人，有諂害之性。

translations.literal: At deathbed she warned Huan and Ye that "Pu's attendant women carry flattery and harmful nature.
translations.idiomatic: Dying she warned them Pu's maids were sly and destructive.

sentences.zh: 身死之後，懼必亂家。

translations.literal: After my death I fear they will disorder the household.
translations.idiomatic: Once I am gone they will wreck this house.

sentences.zh: 汝長大能除之，則吾無恨矣。

translations.literal: If you grow and can remove them I die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Kill them when you can and my ghost rests.

sentences.zh: 」曄年十三，謂兄渙曰：「亡母之言，可以行矣。

translations.literal: "At thirteen Ye told elder brother Huan: "Mother's dying words may be enacted.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen Ye told Huan: "Time to honor Mother's charge.

sentences.zh: 」渙曰：「那可爾！

translations.literal: "Huan said: "How could we do that!
translations.idiomatic: Huan cried: "We cannot!

sentences.zh: 」曄即入室殺侍者，徑出拜墓。

translations.literal: "Ye entered the chamber immediately killed the attendant and went straight to bow at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Ye strode in, cut the woman down, and raced to the grave.

sentences.zh: 舍內大駕，白普。

translations.literal: The household raised great alarm and informed Pu.
translations.idiomatic: The household panicked and told Pu.

sentences.zh: 普怒，遣人追曄。

translations.literal: Pu enraged sent men to pursue Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Pu raged and sent runners after Ye.

sentences.zh: 曄還拜謝曰：「亡母顧命之言，敢受不請擅行之罰。

translations.literal: Ye returned bowing apology: "Mother's dying charge—I dare accept punishment for acting without asking permission.
translations.idiomatic: Ye knelt back: "Mother's last order—I accept whatever penalty for acting unsanctioned.

sentences.zh: 」普心異之，遂不責也。

translations.literal: "Pu marveled inwardly and did not punish.
translations.idiomatic: Pu stared, then spared him.

sentences.zh: 汝南許劭名知人，避地揚州，稱曄有佐世之才。

translations.literal: Runan's Xu Shao famed for judging men, fled to Yangzhou, pronounced Ye had talent to aid the age.
translations.idiomatic: Runan's Xu Shao, refugee in Yangzhou, called Ye fit to steady an empire.

sentences.zh: 揚士多輕俠狡桀，有鄭寶、張多、許乾之屬，各擁部曲。

translations.literal: Yangzhou men were mostly rash bravoes—Zheng Bao, Zhang Duo, Xu Gan types each commanding followings.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou bred swaggering swordsmen—Zheng Bao, Zhang Duo, Xu Gan led private hosts.

sentences.zh: 寶最驍果，才力過人，一方所憚。

translations.literal: Bao was fiercest strength exceeding men—one quarter feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was boldest and strongest—the region dreaded him.

sentences.zh: 欲驅略百姓越赴江表，以曄高族名人，欲強逼曄使唱導此謀。

translations.literal: Wishing to drive commoners south across the river they forced Ye eminent clan celebrity to endorse and lead the scheme.
translations.idiomatic: Plotting to herd civilians south they drafted Ye, eminent name, to bless the march.

sentences.zh: 曄時年二十餘，心內憂之，而未有緣。

translations.literal: Ye then twenty-something worried inwardly yet lacked opening.
translations.idiomatic: Ye past twenty seethed yet saw no lever.

sentences.zh: 會太祖遣使詣州，有所案問。

translations.literal: It happened Grand Progenitor sent envoy to province on investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's investigator arrived.

sentences.zh: 曄往見，為論事勢，要將與歸，駐止數日。

translations.literal: Ye went to see discussed situation insisting envoy stay several days.
translations.idiomatic: Ye met him, argued the stakes, and kept him days.

sentences.zh: 寶果從數百人齎牛酒來候使，曄令家僮將其眾坐中門外，為設酒飯；

translations.literal: Bao indeed brought several hundred men bearing oxen wine to greet envoy; Ye ordered household slaves seat them outside middle gate and set wine food;
translations.idiomatic: Bao marched hundreds with cattle and wine; Ye parked them beyond the inner gate with feast;

sentences.zh: 與寶於內宴飲。

translations.literal: feasted with Bao inside.
translations.idiomatic: then banqueted Bao indoors.

sentences.zh: 密勒健兒，令因行觴而斫寶。

translations.literal: Secretly ordered stalwarts to strike Bao when passing cups.
translations.idiomatic: He told braves to slash Bao mid-toast.

sentences.zh: 寶性不甘酒，視候甚明，觴者不敢發。

translations.literal: Bao by nature did not drink freely; his vigilance was sharp—those passing cups dared not strike.
translations.idiomatic: Bao stayed sober and watched like a hawk—no toast offered an opening for the blade.

sentences.zh: 曄因自引取佩刀斫殺寶，斬其首以令其軍，云：「曹公有令，敢有動者，與寶同罪。

translations.literal: Ye therefore drew his own belt knife, hacked Bao to death, beheaded him to command the army, proclaiming: "Lord Cao orders—whoever moves shares Bao's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Ye snatched his dagger, cut Bao down, lifted his head to the ranks: "Cao Cao commands—stir and you die like Bao.

sentences.zh: 」眾皆驚怖，走還營。

translations.literal: "The crowd panicked and fled back to camp.
translations.idiomatic: The mob bolted for their tents.

sentences.zh: 營有督將精兵數千，懼其為亂，曄即乘寶馬，將家僮數人，詣寶營門，呼其渠帥，喻以禍福，皆叩頭開門內曄。

translations.literal: The camp held several thousand picked troops under overseers; fearing mutiny Ye mounted Bao's fine horse, led several household youths to Bao's gate, summoned their chieftains, explained fortune and ruin—they kowtowed, opened the gates, and admitted Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of veterans ringed the stockade; Ye rode Bao's stallion to the gate with a handful of servants, called out the leaders, pled consequence—and they opened for him knuckling brow.

sentences.zh: 曄撫慰安懷，咸悉悅服，推曄為主。

translations.literal: Ye soothed and reassured them until all gladly submitted and acclaimed Ye as chief.
translations.idiomatic: He calmed them until every blade pledged loyalty and named him leader.

sentences.zh: 曄睹漢室漸微，己為支屬，不欲擁兵，遂委其部曲與廬江太守劉勛。

translations.literal: Seeing the Han house fade and himself a collateral clansman Ye refused to clutch troops and entrusted his following to Liu Xun Administrator of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Han's twilight and royal kinship convinced Ye to shed command—he handed his bands to Lujiang's Liu Xun.

sentences.zh: 勳怪其故，曄曰：「寶無法制，其眾素以鈔略為利，僕宿無資，而整齊之，必懷怨難久，故相與耳。

translations.literal: Xun wondered why; Ye said: "Bao kept no discipline—his men lived by pillage. Your servant lacked wealth to discipline them fairly—they would nurse grudges and not endure—hence I yielded them.
translations.idiomatic: Xun asked; Ye explained: "Those riders lived by robbery; I had no silver to reform them—they would have turned on me—so I passed them along.

sentences.zh: 」時勳兵強於江、淮之間。

translations.literal: "At that time Xun's soldiers were strongest between the Yangzi and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Then Xun dominated the Jiang-Huai corridor.

sentences.zh: 孫策惡之，遣使卑辭厚幣，以書說勳曰：「上繚宗民，數欺下國，忿之有年矣。

translations.literal: Sun Ce hated this and sent envoys with humble phrases and rich gifts, writing Xun: "The Shangliao clans repeatedly insult our humble state—we have nursed resentment years.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce baited him with silk and soft words: "Shangliao bullies us year on year;

sentences.zh: 擊之，路不便，原因大國伐之。

translations.literal: To strike them the roads are awkward—we wish the great state to punish them for us.
translations.idiomatic: the trails punish us—lend your army to chastise them.

sentences.zh: 上繚甚實，得之可以富國，請出兵為外援。

translations.literal: Shangliao is very wealthy; taking it enriches the state—please dispatch troops as outer reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: That county overflows with grain—seize it and your treasury swells; march as our ally.

sentences.zh: 」勳信之，又得策珠寶、葛越，喜悅。

translations.literal: "Xun believed him and moreover received Sun Ce's jewels and fine ge cloth—he rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Xun swallowed the tale and pocketed Ce's pearls and damask—delighted.

sentences.zh: 外內盡賀，而曄獨否。

translations.literal: Court and camp alike congratulated while Ye alone disagreed.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone toasted except Ye.

sentences.zh: 勳問其故，對曰：「上繚雖小，城堅池深，攻難守易，不可旬日而舉，則兵疲於外，而國內虛。

translations.literal: Xun asked his reason; Ye replied: "Though Shangliao is small its walls are firm and moats deep—hard to assault, easy to defend—it cannot fall within ten days; then troops weary abroad while your interior empties.
translations.idiomatic: Ye warned: "Shangliao is a nut—weeks of siege will drain you while your rear goes hollow.

sentences.zh: 策乘虛而襲我，則後不能獨守。

translations.literal: Should Ce exploit the gap and strike us from behind we afterward cannot hold alone.
translations.idiomatic: Ce will stab your spine—you cannot stand alone after.

sentences.zh: 是將軍進屈於敵，退無所歸。

translations.literal: Thus the general advances humbled before the foe and retreats with nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: You march into humiliation and retreat into nowhere.

sentences.zh: 若軍必出，禍今至矣。

translations.literal: If the army must march disaster arrives now.
translations.idiomatic: Sortie now and ruin rides tonight.

sentences.zh: 」勳不從。

translations.literal: "Xun refused to heed.
translations.idiomatic: Xun ignored him.

sentences.zh: 興兵伐上繚，策果襲其後。

translations.literal: He raised troops against Shangliao and Ce indeed struck his rear.
translations.idiomatic: Xun marched north; Ce hit his rear as promised.

sentences.zh: 勳窮踧，遂奔太祖。

translations.literal: Xun was cornered and fled to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Broken, Xun bolted to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 太祖至壽春，時廬江界有山賊陳策，眾數萬人，臨險而守。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor reached Shouchun bandit Chen Ce in Lujiang commanded tens of thousands holding precipitous terrain.
translations.idiomatic: At Shouchun Lujiang hosted Chen Ce's mountain army—myriad fighters on cliffs.

sentences.zh: 先時遣偏將致誅，莫能禽克。

translations.literal: Earlier detached generals sent against him could capture nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier raids never cracked him.

sentences.zh: 太祖問羣下，可伐與不？

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor asked his ministers whether to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao polled the hall: worth striking?

sentences.zh: 咸云：「山峻高而谿谷深隘，守易攻難；

translations.literal: All said: "The peaks soar and ravines narrow—easy to defend, hard to attack;
translations.idiomatic: They answered: "Steep ridges and tight gorges favor defenders;

sentences.zh: 又無之不足為損，得之不足為益。

translations.literal: lacking it costs little harm; gaining it yields little profit.
translations.idiomatic: skip it and we lose little; win it and win little.

sentences.zh: 」曄曰：

translations.literal: "Ye said:
translations.idiomatic: Ye said:

sentences.zh: 策等小豎，因亂赴險，遂相依為強耳，非有爵命威信相伏也。

translations.literal: Chen Ce and ilk are petty boys who fled chaos into narrows and leaned on each other for strength—they possess no patent of rank nor awe to command submission.
translations.idiomatic: Ce is rabble sheltering in rocks—no mandate, no prestige.

sentences.zh: 往者偏將資輕，而中國未夷，故策敢據險以守。

translations.literal: Formerly detached command lacked weight and the Central Plains were unrestful—hence Ce dared cling to the defiles.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser generals and civil war let him squat there.

sentences.zh: 今天下略定，後伏先誅。

translations.literal: Now the realm is largely pacified and rear traitors are executed first.
translations.idiomatic: Today the heartland quiets and rebels hang first.

sentences.zh: 夫畏死趨賞，愚知所同，故廣武君為韓信畫策，謂其威名足以先聲後實而服鄰國也。

translations.literal: Men alike flee death and chase reward—wise or foolish share this—therefore Guangwu Jun plotted for Han Xin that prestige alone could thunder before deeds and humble neighboring states.
translations.idiomatic: All souls chase pay and flee blades—Guangwu Jun told Han Xin fame alone could cow neighbors before blades rose.

sentences.zh: 豈況明公之德，東征西怨，先開賞募，大兵臨之，令宣之日，軍門啟而虜自潰矣。

translations.literal: How much more under my enlightened lord's virtue—eastward campaigns draw western lament—open rewards first, bring main hosts to bear; the day the order sounds camp gates open and captives melt away.
translations.idiomatic: Your virtue makes east march west mourn—publish bounty, slam the army down, and Ce's bands dissolve when trumpets blow.

sentences.zh: 太祖笑曰：「卿言近之！

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor laughed: "Your words hit close!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao grinned: "Near the mark!

sentences.zh: 」遂遣猛將在前，大軍在後，至則克策，如曄所度。

translations.literal: "He dispatched fierce generals forward with main army behind—arriving they conquered Ce exactly as Ye predicted.
translations.idiomatic: He drove vanguard hard, main body behind—Ce fell as Ye forecast.

sentences.zh: 太祖還，辟曄為司空倉曹掾。

translations.literal: On return he summoned Ye as secretary under the Minister of Works granary bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Homeward he named Ye aide in the granary office.

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：太祖徵曄及蔣濟、胡質等五人，皆揚州名士。

translations.literal: 《Master Fu》 records the Grand Progenitor summoned Ye together with Jiang Ji Hu Zhi and five others—all famed Yangzhou gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Master Fu lists five Yangzhou luminaries—Ye, Jiang Ji, Hu Zhi—summoned north.

sentences.zh: 每舍亭傳，未曾不講，所以見重；

translations.literal: At every relay inn they debated without fail—hence they won esteem;
translations.idiomatic: They argued every post-house hence earned notice;

sentences.zh: 內論國邑先賢、禦賊固守、行軍進退之宜，外料敵之變化、彼我虛實、戰爭之術，夙夜不解。

translations.literal: within discussing local worthies bandit defense march doctrine without gauging enemy shifts our mutual weakness war craft—night and day without rest.
translations.idiomatic: inside they rehearsed garrison lore; outside they weighed foe and field—sleepless.

sentences.zh: 而曄獨臥車中，終不一言。

translations.literal: Yet Ye alone lay in his cart and never spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Ye curled in his wagon mute.

sentences.zh: 濟怪而問之，曄答曰：「對明主非精神不接，精神可學而得乎？

translations.literal: Ji marveled and questioned him; Ye answered: "Facing an enlightened lord without focused spirit there is no rapport—can spirit be studied into being?
translations.idiomatic: Ji pressed; Ye said: "A bright sovereign reads presence—can presence be faked from books?

sentences.zh: 」及見太祖，太祖果問揚州先賢，賊之形勢。

translations.literal: "When he met the Grand Progenitor the latter indeed asked about Yangzhou worthies and bandit terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Audience came—Cao Cao quizzed Yangzhou and hills.

sentences.zh: 四人爭對，待次而言，再見如此，太祖每和悅，而曄終不一言。

translations.literal: The four vied to answer taking turns; repeated audiences went thus—the Grand Progenitor always pleasant yet Ye never spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Four tongues raced while Ye stayed silent though Cao Cao smiled.

sentences.zh: 四人笑之。

translations.literal: The four laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: They mocked his silence.

sentences.zh: 後一見太祖止無所復問，曄乃設遠言以動太祖，太祖適知便止。

translations.literal: Later at one audience the Grand Progenitor ceased further questions; Ye then spun a distant topic to move him—the Grand Progenitor grasped it and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Later Cao Cao fell quiet; Ye floated one far-reaching theme—Cao Cao caught it and cut short.

sentences.zh: 若是者三。

translations.literal: Thus thrice.
translations.idiomatic: Three audiences ran that way.

sentences.zh: 其旨趣以為遠言宜徵精神，獨見以盡其機，不宜於猥坐說也。

translations.literal: His intent held that distant speech summons full concentration and sole audience exhausts subtlety—not suited to vulgar bench chatter.
translations.idiomatic: He meant grand themes demand focus and private rooms—not tavern debate.

sentences.zh: 太祖已探見其心矣，坐罷，尋以四人為令，而授曄以心腹之任；

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor had plumbed his heart; after session he soon made the four county magistrates while investing Ye with intimate trust;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao read him—sent the four to county posts and kept Ye at the breast;

sentences.zh: 每有疑事，輒以函問曄，至一夜數十至耳。〉

translations.literal: whenever doubts arose he boxed queries to Ye—sometimes dozens in one night.
translations.idiomatic: midnight brought stacks of sealed questions.

sentences.zh: 太祖征張魯，轉曄為主簿。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Zhang Lu he transferred Ye to chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Against Zhang Lu Ye became chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 既至漢中，山峻難登，軍食頗乏。

translations.literal: Reaching Hanzhong mountains proved steep to climb and army grain grew scarce.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhong cliffs starved the column.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「此妖妄之國耳，何能為有無？

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "This wizard kingdom—what difference make?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sneered: "Shaman country—why bleed for it?

sentences.zh: 吾軍少食，不如速還。

translations.literal: Our army lacks grain—better withdraw quickly.
translations.idiomatic: We are hungry—pull out.

sentences.zh: 」便自引歸，令曄督後諸軍，使以次出。

translations.literal: "He personally led withdrawal ordering Ye to supervise rear echelons to exit in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: He rode ahead telling Ye to stagger the retreat.

sentences.zh: 曄策魯可克，加糧道不繼，雖出，軍猶不能皆全，馳白太祖：「不如致攻。

translations.literal: Ye calculated Lu could be taken yet supply lines failed—even exiting not every soldier would survive—he galloped to report the Grand Progenitor: "Better press the assault.
translations.idiomatic: Ye raced forward: Lu can fall—but retreat starves half the host—attack instead.

sentences.zh: 」遂進兵，多出弩以射其營。

translations.literal: "They advanced deploying many crossbows to rake the camps.
translations.idiomatic: They pushed with bolt storms into Lu's lines.

sentences.zh: 魯奔走，漢中遂平。

translations.literal: Lu fled and Hanzhong was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Lu ran; Hanzhong fell.

sentences.zh: 曄進曰：

translations.literal: Ye pressed saying:
translations.idiomatic: Ye urged:

sentences.zh: 明公以步卒五千，將誅董卓，北破袁紹，南征劉表，九州百郡，十併其八，威震天下，勢慴海外。

translations.literal: My lord with five thousand foot soldiers began by executing Dong Zhuo, crushed Yuan Shao north, campaigned Liu Biao south—among nine provinces hundred commanderies eight tenths obey—awe shakes the realm and might frightens beyond the seas.
translations.idiomatic: From five thousand foot you slew Dong Zhuo, broke Shao, chased Liu Biao—eight parts of nine provinces kneel—terror crosses oceans.

sentences.zh: 今舉漢中，蜀人望風，破膽失守，推此而前，蜀可傳檄而定。

translations.literal: Now Hanzhong falls and Shu men flee at rumor—push forward and Shu may settle by proclamation alone.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhong's capture turns Shu to jelly—one more shove and edicts finish them.

sentences.zh: 劉備，人傑也，有度而遲，得蜀日淺，蜀人未恃也。

translations.literal: Liu Bei is a champion among men—deliberate and slow—holding Shu briefly Shu folk do not yet rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: Bei is heroic yet cautious—new in Shu, hearts still loose.

sentences.zh: 今破漢中，蜀人震恐，其勢自傾。

translations.literal: Hanzhong's loss terrifies Shu—their posture tilts of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Panic already rocks their stance.

sentences.zh: 以公之神明，因其傾而壓之，無不克也。

translations.literal: With my lord's brilliance press their tilt—nothing withstands.
translations.idiomatic: Ride that tilt—nothing stops you.

sentences.zh: 若小緩之，諸葛亮明於治而為相，關羽、張飛勇冠三軍而為將，蜀民既定，據險守要，則不可犯矣。

translations.literal: Delay slightly and Zhuge Liang masters governance as chancellor while Guan Yu and Zhang Fei tower as generals—once Shu folk settle behind narrows they become untouchable.
translations.idiomatic: Hesitate and Zhuge steadies the state while Guan and Zhang bolt the passes—then Shu seals shut.

sentences.zh: 今不取，必為後憂。

translations.literal: Fail to seize now and regret follows.
translations.idiomatic: Skip this hour—pay tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 太祖不從，

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor refused.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao refused.

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：居七日，蜀降者說：「蜀中一日數十驚，備雖斬之而不能安也。

translations.literal: 《Master Fu》 records after seven days Shu defectors reported: "Within Shu dozens of alarms strike daily—though Bei executes culprits calm never returns.
translations.idiomatic: Master Fu adds: seven days later defectors swore Shu shook hourly—Bei's executions bought no peace.

sentences.zh: 」太祖延問曄曰：「今尚可擊不？

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor summoned Ye asking: "May we strike still?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao called Ye: "Still time?

sentences.zh: 」曄曰：「今已小定，未可擊也。」〉

translations.literal: "Ye said: "Now matters have steadied slightly—not fit to strike.)
translations.idiomatic: Ye answered: "Panic faded—too late.)

sentences.zh: 大軍遂還。

translations.literal: The great army therefore returned.
translations.idiomatic: The host marched home.

sentences.zh: 曄自漢中還，為行軍長史，兼領軍。

translations.literal: Ye returning from Hanzhong served acting army chief clerk concurrently commanding the guards.
translations.idiomatic: Ye came back as chief of staff with guard command.

sentences.zh: 延康元年，蜀將孟達率眾降。

translations.literal: First year of Yankang Shu general Meng Da led masses to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yankang 1 brought Meng Da's capitulation.

sentences.zh: 達有容止才觀，文帝甚器愛之，使達為新城太守，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Da possessed dignified bearing and talent—the Wen Emperor prized him greatly, appointing him Administrator of Xincheng with concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi adored Da's polish—made him Xincheng prefect plus attendant.

sentences.zh: 曄以為「達有苟得之心，而恃才好術，必不能感恩懷義。

translations.literal: Ye judged "Da harbors grasping heart relying on talent and schemes—he cannot repay kindness with devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Ye warned Da was greedy genius—gratitude would not bind him.

sentences.zh: 新城與吳、蜀接連，若有變態，為國生患。

translations.literal: Xincheng joins Wu and Shu—should attitudes shift it breeds national peril.
translations.idiomatic: Xincheng touches both rivals—flip allegiance and peril blooms.

sentences.zh: 」文帝竟不易，後達終於叛敗。

translations.literal: "The Wen Emperor never altered course—later Da rebelled and fell.
translations.idiomatic: Pi ignored him—Da revolted and died.

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：初，太祖時，魏諷有重名，自卿相以下皆傾心交之。

translations.literal: 《Master Fu》 records initially under the Grand Progenitor Wei Feng enjoyed towering fame—from ministers downward all befriended him eagerly.
translations.idiomatic: Master Fu recalls Wei Feng's glittering circle under Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 其後孟達去劉備歸文帝，論者多稱有樂毅之量。

translations.literal: Later Meng Da left Liu Bei for the Wen Emperor—commentators mostly compared him to Le Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Later Da fled Bei—critics likened him to Le Yi.

sentences.zh: 曄一見諷、達而皆云必反，卒如其言。〉

translations.literal: Ye one glance at Feng and Da declared both must rebel—ultimately it proved so.
translations.idiomatic: Ye sized Feng and Da once—called both traitors—history agreed.

sentences.zh: 權無故求降，必內有急。

translations.literal: Quan seeks surrender without cause—crisis surely burns within.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan's naked surrender screams inner panic.

sentences.zh: 權前襲殺關羽，取荊州四郡，備怒，必大興師伐之。

translations.literal: Quan earlier ambushed Guan Yu and seized four Jing commanderies—Bei rages and must raise great army against him.
translations.idiomatic: Quan slew Guan Yu and stole four districts—Bei will thunder south.

sentences.zh: 外有強寇，眾心不安，又恐中國承其釁而伐之，故委地求降，一以卻中國之兵，二則假中國之援，以強其眾而疑敵人。

translations.literal: Outside lurks mighty foe; hearts lack peace; fearing the Central Plains would exploit the breach they yield territory begging surrender—first to beat back Wei troops second to borrow Wei aid thereby stiffening their masses and baffling the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Wu fears Wei mid strike—so they kneel to stall your blades and borrow your banner to steady Wu's spine.

sentences.zh: 權善用兵，見策知變，其計必出於此。

translations.literal: Quan deploys soldiers skillfully reads stratagem and adapts—his plan must stem from this.
translations.idiomatic: Quan is fox enough—this is textbook Sun Ce craft.

sentences.zh: 今天下三分，中國十有其八。

translations.literal: Now the realm divides three ways—the Central Plains holds eight tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Three kingdoms stand—Wei owns eight in ten.

sentences.zh: 吳、蜀各保一州，阻山依水，有急相救，此小國之利也。

translations.literal: Wu and Shu each guard one province blocking mountains trusting rivers rushing mutual aid—such is small state advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Shu cling to single provinces—mountains, rivers, mutual rescue—the small-power playbook.

sentences.zh: 今還自相攻，天亡之也。

translations.literal: Now they turn weapons on each other—Heaven destroys them.
translations.idiomatic: They claw each other—Heaven hands you the opening.

sentences.zh: 宜大興師，徑渡江襲其內。

translations.literal: Fit to raise great army ford straight across strike their vitals.
translations.idiomatic: Mobilize and ford straight into their belly.

sentences.zh: 蜀攻其外，我襲其內，吳之亡不出旬月矣。

translations.literal: Shu assaults without—we strike within—Wu cannot survive ten months.
translations.idiomatic: Shu pins the front—you dagger the rear—Wu dies inside a season.

sentences.zh: 吳亡則蜀孤。

translations.literal: Wu gone Shu stands isolated.
translations.idiomatic: Wu falls—Shu stands alone.

sentences.zh: 若割吳半，蜀固不能久存，況蜀得其外，我得其內乎！

translations.literal: Halve Wu and Shu cannot long endure—how much more when Shu seizes their exterior and we seize their interior!
translations.idiomatic: Carve half of Wu and Shu suffocates—worse when Shu grabs skin while you take organs!

sentences.zh: 〈帝曰：「人稱臣降而伐之，疑天下欲來者心，必以為懼，其殆不可！

translations.literal: (The Emperor said: "If subjects surrender and we attack we sow doubt in every heart wishing to come—terror spreads—surely impermissible!
translations.idiomatic: (Cao Pi objected: "Strike a kneeling foe and future capitulators tremble—

sentences.zh: 孤何不且受吳降，而襲蜀之後乎？

translations.literal: Why do I not accept Wu's surrender while striking Shu from behind?
translations.idiomatic: why not hug Wu's pledge then stab Shu's rear?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「蜀遠吳近，又聞中國伐之，便還軍，不能止也。

translations.literal: "He answered: "Shu lies distant Wu near—hearing Central Plains campaigns they withdraw armies unstoppable.
translations.idiomatic: Ye replied: "Shu sits far—news of your march makes Liu Bei wheel home unstoppable.

sentences.zh: 今備已怒，故興兵擊吳，聞我伐吳，知吳必亡，必喜而進與我爭割吳地，必不改計抑怒救吳，必然勢也。

translations.literal: Now Bei already furious raises troops striking Wu—hearing we strike Wu knowing Wu must fall he gladly advances contesting Wu territory with us—surely he will not reverse plan suppress wrath to rescue Wu—such posture follows necessity.
translations.idiomatic: Bei already burns to crush Wu—learn you strike Wu and he hurries to carve corpse—he will never swallow rage to save Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽，遂受吳降，即拜權為吳王。

translations.literal: "The Emperor refused to listen—accepted Wu surrender at once enfeoffing Quan King of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Pi brushed Ye aside—accepted Wu and crowned Sun Quan king.

sentences.zh: 曄又進曰：〉

translations.literal: Ye advanced further saying:
translations.idiomatic: Ye pressed again:

sentences.zh: 不可。

translations.literal: Unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: No.

sentences.zh: 先帝征伐，天下兼其八，威震海內，陛下受禪即真，德合天地，聲暨四遠，此實然之勢，非卑臣頌言也。

translations.literal: Former emperor's campaigns united eight tenths of the realm awe filling seas—Your Majesty receiving abdication embodies virtue matching heaven and earth fame reaching four quarters—such momentum stands fact not base minister's praise.
translations.idiomatic: Martial Emperor seized eight tenths—you inherit mandate joining heaven—no flattery, plain physics.

sentences.zh: 權雖有雄才，故漢驃騎將軍南昌侯耳，官輕勢卑。

translations.literal: Though Quan possesses heroic talent he remains merely Han's former General of Agile Cavalry Marquis of Nanchang—office light position low.
translations.idiomatic: Quan remains an old Han general—rank thin.

sentences.zh: 士民有畏中國心，不可強迫與成所謀也。

translations.literal: Officers and people harbor fear of the Central Plains—cannot coerce them into completing supposed conspiracy.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's gentry still dread Wei—you cannot force instant loyalty.

sentences.zh: 不得已受其降，可進其將軍號，封十萬戶侯，不可即以為王也。

translations.literal: Forced to accept surrender promote his general's title enfeoff hundred-thousand-household marquis—must not instantly make him king.
translations.idiomatic: If you must accept, raise him general and fat marquis—not king.

sentences.zh: 夫王位，去天子一階耳，其禮秩服御相亂也。

translations.literal: For king rank stands one degree below Son of Heaven—ritual grades robes equipage overlap.
translations.idiomatic: King brushes the throne—regalia collides with imperial ritual.

sentences.zh: 彼直為侯，江南士民未有君臣之義也。

translations.literal: Were he merely marquis the Jiangnan gentry and commoners would yet lack lord-minister duty.
translations.idiomatic: Keep him a mere marquis and Wu's people owe you no fealty.

sentences.zh: 我信其偽降，就封殖之，崇其位號，定其君臣，是為虎傅翼也。

translations.literal: Should we trust sham surrender, nurture him with ennoblement, elevate title-rank, fix lord-minister bond—we add wings to a tiger.
