translations.literal: At that time the main army campaigned in Jingzhou and encountered plague—only General Zhang Xi was sent alone with one thousand cavalry to pass through and take command of Runan troops to lift the siege—and plague struck again.
translations.idiomatic: The main host died to plague in Jing; only Zhang Xi rode north with a thousand horse to sweep Runan levies to Hefei—and sickness followed him.

sentences.zh: 濟乃密白刺史偽得喜書，雲步騎四萬已到雩婁，遣主簿迎喜。

translations.literal: Ji therefore secretly informed the Inspector forging receipt of Xi's letter stating forty thousand foot and horse had reached Yulou and ordering the chief clerk to welcome Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Ji forged orders to the prefect: Xi's forty thousand were at Yulou—send clerks to greet them.

sentences.zh: 三部使齎書語城中守將，一部得入城，二部為賊所得。

translations.literal: Three parties carried letters to speak with defenders in the city—one party entered the city; two parties fell to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Three messengers ran letters—one slipped inside; Sun Quan seized two.

sentences.zh: 權信之，遽燒圍走，城用得全。

translations.literal: Quan believed it, hastily burned the siege lines and fled—the city was thereby preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Quan swallowed the bait, torched his lines, and fled—Hefei stood.

sentences.zh: 明年使於譙，太祖問濟曰：「昔孤與袁本初對官渡，徙燕、白馬民，民不得走，賊亦不敢鈔。

translations.literal: The next year Ji was sent to Qiao; the Grand Progenitor asked Ji: "Formerly I opposed Yuan Benchu at Guandu and moved the people of Yan and Baima—the people could not flee and the bandits also dared not raid.
translations.idiomatic: Next year at Qiao Cao Cao asked: "At Guandu I evacuated Yan and Baima—foes dared not loot the roads.

sentences.zh: 今欲徙淮南民，何如？

translations.literal: Now I wish to move the Huainan people—what say you?
translations.idiomatic: Should I empty Huainan?

sentences.zh: 」濟對曰：「是時兵弱賊強，不徙必失之。

translations.literal: "Ji replied: "Then troops were weak and bandits strong—not moving would surely lose them.
translations.idiomatic: Ji answered: "Then we were weak—flight saved lives.

sentences.zh: 自破袁紹，北拔柳城，南向江、漢，荊州交臂，威震天下，民無他志。

translations.literal: Since destroying Yuan Shao, taking Liucheng north, thrusting south toward the Jiang and Han with Jingzhou within grasp, awe shakes the realm—the people harbor no other allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Since Shao fell you hold north and south—commoners fear you, not Wu.

sentences.zh: 然百姓懷土，實不樂徙，懼必不安。

translations.literal: Yet the commoners cling to their soil and truly dislike removal—they will surely grow restless.
translations.idiomatic: Yet peasants love home—mass deportation breeds panic.

sentences.zh: 」太祖不從，而江、淮間十餘萬眾，皆驚走吳。

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor refused—and over one hundred thousand folk between the Jiang and Huai fled in alarm into Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao refused—and a hundred thousand souls bolted east to Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 後濟使詣鄴，太祖迎見大笑曰：「本但欲使避賊，乃更驅盡之。

translations.literal: Later when Ji was sent to Ye the Grand Progenitor welcomed him laughing: "I meant only to help them escape bandits—instead I drove them all away.
translations.idiomatic: Later at Ye Cao Cao laughed: "I meant shelter—I scattered every farmer.

sentences.zh: 」拜濟丹陽太守。

translations.literal: "He appointed Ji Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He named Ji Danyang prefect.

sentences.zh: 大軍南征還，以溫恢為揚州刺史，濟為別駕。

translations.literal: When the great army returned south Wen Hui was made Inspector of Yangzhou and Ji aide.
translations.idiomatic: The southern march ended with Wen Hui as Yangzhou inspector and Ji as aide.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「季子為臣，吳宜有君。

translations.literal: Order stated: "With Jizi serving as minister Wu ought to have its lord.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Minister Jizi implies Wu needs its shepherd.

sentences.zh: 今君還州，吾無憂矣。

translations.literal: Now that you return to the province I have no anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Your return puts my mind at ease.

sentences.zh: 」民有誣告濟為謀叛主率者，太祖聞之，指前令與左將軍於禁、沛相封仁等曰：「蔣濟寧有此事！

translations.literal: When commoners falsely accused Ji of plotting rebellion as ringleader the Grand Progenitor hearing pointed to his earlier order before Left General Yu Jin and Pei Chancellor Feng Ren saying: "Could Jiang Ji do such a thing!
translations.idiomatic: When malice accused Ji of leading revolt Cao Cao waved his old warrant at Yu Jin and Feng Ren: "Ji rebel? Impossible!

sentences.zh: 有此事，吾為不知人也。

translations.literal: Were there such a matter I would prove ignorant of men.
translations.idiomatic: If true I cannot read character.

sentences.zh: 此必愚民樂亂，妄引之耳。

translations.literal: This must be foolish folk delighting in chaos falsely dragging him in.
translations.idiomatic: Mob spite invented the plot.

sentences.zh: 」促理出之。

translations.literal: He urged settlement and release.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Ji cleared.

sentences.zh: 辟為丞相主簿西曹屬。

translations.literal: Ji was summoned Chancellor chief clerk western bureau subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Ji entered the chancellery as western bureau clerk.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「舜舉皋陶，不仁者遠；

translations.literal: Order stated: "When Shun raised Gao Yao the unkind departed;
translations.idiomatic: The charge quoted Shun elevating Gao Yao—villains fled;

sentences.zh: 臧否得中，望於賢屬矣。

translations.literal: to hit mean between praise and blame rests with worthy aides.
translations.idiomatic: fair judgment now sits with your bench.

sentences.zh: 」關羽圍樊、襄陽。

translations.literal: Guan Yu besieged Fan and Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu ringed Fan and Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 太祖以漢帝在許，近賊，欲徙都。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor because the Han emperor was at Xu near the enemy wished to move the capital.
translations.idiomatic: With the emperor at Xu hard by Yu Cao Cao wished to relocate court.

sentences.zh: 司馬宣王及濟說太祖曰：「於禁等為水所沒，非戰攻之失，於國家大計未足有損。

translations.literal: Sima Yi and Ji persuaded the Grand Progenitor: "Yu Jin and others were drowned by flood—not fault of battle assault—and does not yet harm the state's grand plan.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi and Ji argued floods drowned Yu Jin—that misfortune need not uproot the court.

sentences.zh: 劉備、孫權，外親內疏，關羽得志，權必不原也。

translations.literal: Liu Bei and Sun Quan are kin outwardly yet estranged inwardly—should Guan Yu succeed Quan will surely not forgive.
translations.idiomatic: Bei and Quan fake friendship—let Yu win and Quan will stab his back.

sentences.zh: 可遣人勸躡其後，許割江南以封權，則樊圍自解。

translations.literal: Dispatch envoys urging someone to tread his rear—promise to cede Jiangnan and enfeoff Quan—then the Fan siege resolves itself.
translations.idiomatic: Urge Quan to raid Yu's rear—promise him south of the river—and Fan cracks.

sentences.zh: 」太祖如其言。

translations.literal: "The Grand Progenitor followed his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao agreed.

sentences.zh: 權聞之，即引兵西襲公安、江陵。

translations.literal: Quan hearing immediately led troops west striking Gong'an and Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Quan swept west on Gong'an and Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 羽遂見禽。

translations.literal: Yu was then captured.
translations.idiomatic: Yu fell captive.

sentences.zh: 文帝即王位，轉為相國長史。

translations.literal: When the Wen Emperor assumed kingship Ji transferred to chief clerk of the Chancellor of State.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi made Ji secretary to the imperial chancellor.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，出為東中郎將。

translations.literal: Upon ascending Ji exited as General of the Household East of Center.
translations.idiomatic: At coronation Ji became General East of Center.

sentences.zh: 濟請留，詔曰：「高祖歌曰『安得猛士守四方』！

translations.literal: Ji requested to remain; edict said: "The High Ancestor sang 'how obtain fierce warriors to guard the four directions'!
translations.idiomatic: Ji begged to stay in court; Pi cited Gaozu's song—who guards the marches?

sentences.zh: 天下未寧，要須良臣以鎮邊境。

translations.literal: The realm is not yet tranquil—you must have good ministers to steady the borders.
translations.idiomatic: The empire still boils—send proven hands to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 如其無事，乃還鳴玉，未為後也。

translations.literal: When nothing threatens return jade chimes sounding—not considered late.
translations.idiomatic: Peace will bring you home to tinkling pendants soon enough.

sentences.zh: 」濟上萬機論，帝善之。

translations.literal: "Ji submitted treatise on myriad affairs—the Emperor praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's essay on governance pleased Rui.

sentences.zh: 入為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He entered as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He became Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 時有詔，詔征南將軍夏侯尚曰：「卿腹心重將，特當任使。

translations.literal: At that time an edict told General Who Conquers the South Xiahou Shang: "You are trusted core general specially entrusted missions.
translations.idiomatic: An edict told Xiahou Shang: "You are my intimate blade.

sentences.zh: 恩施足死，惠愛可懷。

translations.literal: Kind grace suffices that men die for you; benevolent love wins devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Mercy earns lives; love earns hearts.

sentences.zh: 作威作福，殺人活人。

translations.literal: Make awe make fortune—kill men enliven men.
translations.idiomatic: Wield life and death.

sentences.zh: 」尚以示濟。

translations.literal: Shang showed it to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Shang showed Ji the parchment.

sentences.zh: 濟既至，帝問曰；

translations.literal: When Ji arrived the Emperor asked;
translations.idiomatic: Ji entered audience;

sentences.zh: 「卿所聞見天下風教何如？

translations.literal: "What you have heard and seen of customs and instruction across the realm?
translations.idiomatic: "How reads the moral climate?

sentences.zh: 」濟對曰：「未有他善，但見亡國之語耳。

translations.literal: "Ji replied: "No other goodness—only phrases fit for fallen states.
translations.idiomatic: Ji answered: "I hear only words fit for dying kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 」帝忿然作色而問其故，濟具以答，因曰：「夫『作威作福』，書之明誡。

translations.literal: "The Emperor flushed angrily asking reason; Ji answered fully saying: "Now 'make awe make fortune' is Documents' clear warning.
translations.idiomatic: Rui reddened; Ji quoted the Shangshu—such lines doom dynasties.

sentences.zh: 『天子無戲言』，古人所慎。

translations.literal: 'Son of Heaven utters no jest'—what ancients feared.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's son speaks once—no joking.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下察之！

translations.literal: Only Your Majesty examine!
translations.idiomatic: Weigh it, Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」於是帝意解，遣追取前詔。

translations.literal: "Thereupon the Emperor's anger eased and he dispatched riders to retrieve the prior edict.
translations.idiomatic: Rui cooled and recalled the order.

sentences.zh: 時中書監、令號為專任，濟上疏曰：

translations.literal: At that time Palace Secretariat Supervisor and Director were called sole power—Ji memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: When secretariat chiefs monopolized favor Ji wrote:

sentences.zh: 大臣太重者國危，左右太親者身蔽，古之至戒也。

translations.literal: Too-heavy ministers imperil the state; too-intimate attendants blind the ruler—ancients' gravest warning.
translations.idiomatic: Top-heavy ministers and whispering favorites ruined ages past.

sentences.zh: 往者大臣秉事，外內扇動。

translations.literal: Formerly ministers grasped affairs and inside and outside stirred together.
translations.idiomatic: Once magnates hijacked policy inside and out churned.

sentences.zh: 陛下卓然自覽萬機，莫不祗肅。

translations.literal: Your Majesty outstandingly personally reads myriad threads—none fail reverence.
translations.idiomatic: You alone now hold the files—good.

sentences.zh: 夫大臣非不忠也，然威權在下，則眾心慢上，勢之常也。

translations.literal: Ministers are not disloyal yet when awe lodges below the multitude slights the throne—that tendency holds.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers stay loyal yet power below breeds contempt above—that is habit.

sentences.zh: 陛下既已察之於大臣，原無忘於左右。

translations.literal: Your Majesty already discerned this among ministers—pray forget not your attendants.
translations.idiomatic: You vet ministers—vet valets too.

sentences.zh: 左右忠正遠慮，未必賢於大臣，至於便辟取合，或能工之。

translations.literal: Attendants loyal and far-sighted are not necessarily worthier than ministers—yet for slick flattery winning favor some excel.
translations.idiomatic: Pages may lack ministerial virtue yet excel at pleasing ears.

sentences.zh: 今外所言，輒云中書，雖使恭慎不敢外交，但有此名，猶惑世俗。

translations.literal: Now outsiders speak always of Palace Secretariat—even ordered respectful not to mingle abroad merely having this name still misleads the world.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor pins every whisper on the secretariat—danger enough without scandal.

sentences.zh: 況實握事要，日在目前，儻因疲倦之間有所割制，眾臣見其能推移於事，即亦因時而向之。

translations.literal: Moreover truly grasping essentials daily before your eyes—should weariness invite delegated slices ministers seeing ability to shift affairs will lean with the hour.
translations.idiomatic: They hold real levers under your eyes—fatigue lets them carve policy until the hall courts them.

sentences.zh: 一有此端，因當內設自完，以此眾語，私招所交，為之內援。

translations.literal: Once that crack opens they fortify within trading gossip privately recruiting allies as inner support.
translations.idiomatic: One foothold breeds cabals—secret allies sprout inside.

sentences.zh: 若此，臧否毀譽，必有所興，功負賞罰，必有所易；

translations.literal: If so praise and slander stir—merit fault reward punishment invert;
translations.idiomatic: Then rumor owns appointments—rewards punish wrong men;

sentences.zh: 直道而上者或壅，曲附左右者反達。

translations.literal: straight paths stall while crooks beside the throne rise.
translations.idiomatic: honest voices choke—flatterers beside you soar.

sentences.zh: 因微而入，緣形而出，意所狎信，不復猜覺。

translations.literal: Following subtle entries and shaped exits those you fondly trust cease guessing.
translations.idiomatic: Trust creeps in unseen until favorites blind you.

sentences.zh: 此宜聖智所當早聞，外以經意，則形際自見。

translations.literal: Sage wisdom ought hear this early—apply outward vigilance and symptoms show.
translations.idiomatic: Wise kings spot it early—steady intent abroad and the tumor surfaces.

sentences.zh: 或恐朝臣畏言不合而受左右之怨，莫適以聞。

translations.literal: Perhaps court ministers fear speech mismatch bringing attendants' resentment—none fit to report.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers fear palace spite—silence spreads.

sentences.zh: 臣竊亮陛下潛神默思，公聽並觀，若事有未盡於理而物有未周於用，將改曲易調，遠與黃、唐角功，近昭武、文之跡，豈近習而已哉！

translations.literal: Your servant trusts Your Majesty ponders in silence listens broadly views together—should principle lack completeness or utility lack thoroughness you will bend tune—far rival Huang Di Tang merit near mirror Wu Wen traces—how mere intimate habit!
translations.idiomatic: Trust you meditate—if policy cracks you will retune—rivaling Huang Tang abroad and mirroring Wu Wen at home—not petty palace habit!

sentences.zh: 然人君猶不可悉天下事以適己明，當有所付。

translations.literal: Yet even a lord cannot exhaust all realm affairs to suit personal clarity—something must be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: No emperor reads every file—delegation stays.

sentences.zh: 三官任一臣，非周公旦之忠，又非管夷吾之公，則有弄機敗官之弊。

translations.literal: Three offices in one hand—without Duke of Zhou's loyalty nor Guan Zhong's fairness—breeds manipulation ruining office.
translations.idiomatic: One man holding triple seals without Zhou loyalty or Guan fairness invites cabal rot.

sentences.zh: 當今柱石之士雖少，至於行稱一州，智效一官，忠信竭命，各奉其職，可並驅策，不使聖明之朝有專吏之名也。

translations.literal: Present pillar gentlemen though few include men praised in one province wise in one post loyal exhausting mandate each holding office—drive them together—do not let a sagely court bear sole-clerk fame.
translations.idiomatic: You still have provincial talents—parallel commands beat one imperial clerk.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「夫骨鯁之臣，人主之所仗也。

translations.literal: Edict said: "Bone-straight ministers are what the lord relies upon.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial reply: "The throne needs spines.

sentences.zh: 濟才兼文武，服勤盡節，每軍國大事，輒有奏議，忠誠奮發，吾甚壯之。

translations.literal: Ji combines civil and military talent devoted diligent exhausting integrity—each army-state crisis draws memorials—loyalty fervent—I greatly admire.
translations.idiomatic: Ji marries brush and blade—loyal counsel every crisis—I honor him.

sentences.zh: 」就遷為護軍將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was promoted General Who Guards the Army plus Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Guard general with attendant sash.

sentences.zh: 〈司馬彪《戰略》曰：太和六年，明帝遣平州刺史田豫乘海渡，幽州刺史王雄陸道，並攻遼東。

translations.literal: Sima Biao Strategic Notes: Taihe six Ming Emperor dispatched Pingzhou Inspector Tian Yu by sea and Youzhou Inspector Wang Xiong by land jointly attacking Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao records Taihe six: Tian Yu sailed Pingzhou while Wang Xiong marched Youzhou against Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 蔣濟諫曰：「凡非相吞之國，不侵叛之臣，不宜輕伐。

translations.literal: Jiang Ji remonstrated: "Generally states not swallowing each other and ministers not rebel-invading ought not be lightly campaigned.
translations.idiomatic: Ji warned: never strike neighbors who pose no swallowing threat.

sentences.zh: 伐之而不制，是驅使為賊。

translations.literal: Campaign yet fail to control drives them to become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Half wars forge enemies.

sentences.zh: 故曰『虎狼當路，不治狐狸。

translations.literal: Hence says 'tigers and wolves block the road—do not bother with foxes.
translations.idiomatic: Proverb: tigers own the road—ignore foxes.

sentences.zh: 先除大害，小害自已』。

translations.literal: First remove great harm—small harm stops itself'.
translations.idiomatic: Cut the big predator—vermin quit.

sentences.zh: 今海表之地，累世委質，歲選計考，不乏職貢。

translations.literal: Now lands beyond the seas for generations have pledged substance yearly examinations presenting tribute without failing duty.
translations.idiomatic: The coast pays tribute on schedule—loyal generations.

sentences.zh: 議者先之，正使一舉便克，得其民不足益國，得其財不足為富；

translations.literal: Debaters prioritize them—even granting one stroke conquers—gaining people insufficient to enrich state gaining wealth insufficient to enrich treasury;
translations.idiomatic: Victory wins neither manpower nor treasure worth the cost;

sentences.zh: 儻不如意，是為結怨失信也。

translations.literal: perhaps not as wished then becomes knotting resentment losing trust.
translations.idiomatic: failure buys hatred and broken faith.

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽，豫行竟無成而還。〉

translations.literal: "The Emperor refused—Yu's expedition accomplished nothing and returned.)
translations.idiomatic: Rui ignored him—Tian Yu sailed home empty.)

sentences.zh: 景初中，外勤征役，內務宮室，怨曠者多，而年穀飢儉。

translations.literal: Mid Jingchu outward diligent campaigns inward palace tasks many resentful separated yearly grain famine scarcity.
translations.idiomatic: Mid Jingchu paired foreign wars with palace builds—troops languished while granaries failed.

sentences.zh: 濟上疏曰：

translations.literal: Ji memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Ji wrote:

sentences.zh: 陛下方當恢崇前緒，光濟遺業，誠未得高枕而治也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought expand prior threads brighten leftover enterprise—truly cannot yet high-pillow govern.
translations.idiomatic: You inherit a half-built throne—no time to nap.

sentences.zh: 今雖有十二州，至於民數，不過漢時一大郡。

translations.literal: Now though twelve provinces the people count does not surpass one great Han commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve provinces hold fewer mouths than one Han metropolis.

sentences.zh: 二賊未誅，宿兵邊陲，且耕且戰，怨曠積年。

translations.literal: Two bandits not executed—troops linger borders farming fighting—resentful separation piles years.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Shu live—frontier armies farm-fight—homes empty year on year.

sentences.zh: 宗廟宮室，百事草創，農桑者少，衣食者多，今其所急，唯當息耗百姓，不至甚弊。

translations.literal: Ancestral temples palace hundred affairs grass founding farming mulberry few clothing food many—now urgent ought rest diminishing common people not reach extreme ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Shrines and halls rise while farms shrink—ease the people before they break.

sentences.zh: 弊攰之民，儻有水旱，百萬之眾，不為國用。

translations.literal: Ruined weary people—should flood drought strike—million masses will not serve state use.
translations.idiomatic: Broken peasants plus drought turn millions useless to the throne.

sentences.zh: 凡使民必須農隙，不奪其時。

translations.literal: Generally employing people must rely on farming gaps—not seize their seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée belongs after harvest—never steal spring.

sentences.zh: 夫欲大興功之君，先料其民力而燠休之。

translations.literal: Lords wishing great works first gauge people strength and comforts them.
translations.idiomatic: Great builders nurse labor before breaking ground.

sentences.zh: 句踐養胎以待用，昭王卹病以雪仇，故能以弱燕服強齊，羸越滅勁吳。

translations.literal: Goujian nurtured births awaiting use; King Zhao pitied sickness to avenge shame—therefore weak Yan subdued strong Qi wasted Yue destroyed vigorous Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Goujian bred soldiers; Zhao pitied the sick—weak Yan beat Qi and lean Yue swallowed Wu.

sentences.zh: 今二敵不攻不滅，不事即侵，當身不除，百世之責也。

translations.literal: Now two foes not attacked not destroyed—ignore them and they invade—fail to remove in your lifetime blame falls hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Leave Wu and Shu—they raid tomorrow—your heirs curse you.

sentences.zh: 以陛下聖明神武之略，捨其緩者，專心討賊，臣以為無難矣。

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's sagely divine martial stratagem abandon lesser tasks concentrate heart punishing bandits—your servant thinks no difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Shelve palace whims—focus spears on Shu-Wu—easy win.

sentences.zh: 又歡娛之耽，害於精爽；

translations.literal: Moreover pleasure indulgence harms essence brightness;
translations.idiomatic: Hedonism dulls the spirit;

sentences.zh: 神太用則竭，形太勞則弊。

translations.literal: spirit overused exhausts—form overlabored ruins.
translations.idiomatic: mind burns out—body breaks.

sentences.zh: 原大簡賢妙，足以充『百斯男』者。

translations.literal: Wish greatly select worthy subtle sufficient to supply 'hundred heirs'.
translations.idiomatic: Cull harem to worthy mothers fit for royal sons.

sentences.zh: 其冗散未齒，且悉分出，務在清靜。

translations.literal: Those redundant scattered unranked temporarily all divide out striving in purity quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Spin idle attendants out—keep inner chambers lean.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「微護軍，吾弗聞斯言也。」

translations.literal: Edict said: "Without Guard Army I would not have heard these words."
translations.idiomatic: Rui answered: "Without Ji I would miss this truth."

sentences.zh: 〈《漢晉春秋》曰：公孫淵聞魏將來討，復稱臣於孫權，乞兵自救。

translations.literal: Han-Jin Spring and Autumn: Gongsun Yuan hearing Wei generals coming to punish again declared subject to Sun Quan begging troops self-rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Han-Jin Spring notes Yuan hearing Wei's march knelt again to Quan for rescue.

sentences.zh: 帝問濟：「孫權其救遼東乎？

translations.literal: Emperor asked Ji: "Will Sun Quan rescue Liaodong?
translations.idiomatic: Rui asked whether Quan would sail north.

sentences.zh: 」濟曰：「彼知官備以固，利不可得，深入則非力所能，淺入則勞而無獲；

translations.literal: "Ji said: "They know official defenses firm profit unobtainable—deep thrust exceeds strength—shallow thrust wearies without gain;
translations.idiomatic: Ji said: "Quan sees strong walls—deep raids starve—shallow raids earn nothing;

sentences.zh: 權雖子弟在危，猶將不動，況異域之人，兼以往者之辱乎！

translations.literal: Quan though sons and nephews in peril still will not move—how much more foreign land people compounded by former humiliation!
translations.idiomatic: Quan would not hazard kin—why risk treasure for Yuan's slight after past insult?

sentences.zh: 今所以外揚此聲者，譎其行人疑於我，我之不克，冀折後事已耳。

translations.literal: Now the reason they broadcast this rumor abroad is to make envoys doubt us; should we fail to conquer they hope only to unsettle later stages.
translations.idiomatic: They trumpet rescue to spook our scouts—just in case we stall.

sentences.zh: 然沓渚之間，去淵尚遠，若大軍相持，事不速決，則權之淺規，或能輕兵掩襲，未可測也。」〉

translations.literal: Yet between Taizhu and Yuan the distance remains large—should main armies deadlock without swift decision Quan's shallow probe might send light troops on a sudden raid—impossible to predict.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhu lies far from Liaodong—a drawn duel invites Quan to slash our flank—who can chart that raid?

sentences.zh: 初，侍中高堂隆論郊祀事，以魏為舜後，推舜配天。

translations.literal: Initially Attendant Gaotang Long debated suburban sacrifice holding Wei as heirs of Shun and pairing Shun with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Long argued Wei descended from Shun for rites.

sentences.zh: 濟以為舜本姓媯，其苗曰田，非曹之先，著文以追詰隆。

translations.literal: Ji held Shun's original surname was Gui his descendants took Tian—not Cao's ancestors—and composed text pressing Long.
translations.idiomatic: Ji insisted Shun's line was Gui-turned-Tian—not Cao—and wrote to rebuke Long.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案蔣濟立郊議稱曹騰碑文云「曹氏族出自邾」，《魏書》述曹氏胤緒亦如之。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi notes Jiang Ji's suburban memorial cited Cao Teng's stele saying "the Cao clan came out of Zhu"; the Book of Wei traces Cao genealogy the same way.
translations.idiomatic: Pei cites Ji quoting Cao Teng's tablet—Caos stem from Zhu per Wei records.

sentences.zh: 魏武作家傳，自云曹叔振鐸之後。

translations.literal: Martial Emperor composed a house genealogy calling himself descendant of royal uncle Zhenduo of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's family memoir claims Duke Zhenduo's blood.

sentences.zh: 故陳思王作武帝誄曰：「於穆武皇，冑稷胤周。

translations.literal: Hence Prince Si of Chen composed the Martial Emperor's dirge saying "Ah solemn Martial Sovereign helmet-line traces Hou Ji continuing Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi's elegy ties Wu Di to Hou Ji and Zhou.

sentences.zh: 」此其不同者也。

translations.literal: This is where they disagree.
translations.idiomatic: The traditions collide here.

sentences.zh: 及至景初，明帝從高堂隆議，謂魏為舜後，後魏為禪晉文，稱「昔我皇祖有虞」，則其異彌甚。

translations.literal: By Jingchu Ming Emperor accepted Gaotang Long's theory deeming Wei Shun's heirs; later Wei's abdication document to Jin spoke "formerly our august ancestor You Yu"—the discrepancy widens.
translations.idiomatic: Rui followed Long—yet Jin abdication hymns Caos as You Yu—contradiction deepens.

sentences.zh: 尋濟難隆，及與尚書繆襲往反，並有理據，文多不載。

translations.literal: Examining Ji's debate with Long and written exchanges with Minister Mu Xi both carried evidence—most text omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's letters to Long and Mu Xi argued tightly—editors trimmed them.

sentences.zh: 濟亦未能定氏族所出，但謂「魏非舜後而橫祀非族，降黜太祖，不配正天，皆為繆妄」。

translations.literal: Ji still could not pin the clan's origin yet insisted "Wei is not Shun's heir yet sacrifices stray lines demoting the Grand Progenitor from pairing orthodox Heaven—all delusion."
translations.idiomatic: Ji denied Shun blood—foreign altars demoted Cao Cao from Heaven's match.

sentences.zh: 然於時竟莫能正。

translations.literal: Yet none at the time could settle it.
translations.idiomatic: No court verdict landed.

sentences.zh: 濟又難：鄭玄注祭法云「有虞以上尚德，禘郊祖宗，配用有德，自夏已下，稍用其姓氏」。

translations.literal: Ji further challenged Zheng Xuan's gloss on Sacrifice Law: "Before You Yu they prized virtue—grand offerings matched the worthy—from Xia onward they gradually used surnames."
translations.idiomatic: Ji attacked Zheng's reading of the Offering canon.

sentences.zh: 濟曰：「夫虯龍神於獺，獺自祭其先，不祭虯龍也。

translations.literal: Ji said: "Horned dragons outrank otters yet otters sacrifice their own ancestors—not dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Ji likened it: otters honor otters—not dragons.

sentences.zh: 騏驎白虎仁於豺，豺自祭其先，不祭騏虎也。

translations.literal: Qilin and white tiger outrank wolves yet wolves sacrifice their own ancestors—not qilin or tigers.
translations.idiomatic: Unicorns top wolves—wolves still worship wolves.

sentences.zh: 如玄之說，有虞已上，豺獺之不若邪？

translations.literal: On Xuan's logic were men before You Yu worse than wolves and otters?
translations.idiomatic: Did sage kings rank below beasts?

sentences.zh: 臣以為祭法所云，見疑學者久矣，鄭玄不考正其違而就通其義。

translations.literal: Your servant believes the Sacrifice Law passage has long puzzled scholars—Xuan never corrected the clash yet glossed it smooth.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars doubt that clause—Zheng papered cracks.

sentences.zh: 」濟豺獺之譬，雖似俳諧，然其義旨，有可求焉。〉

translations.literal: Though Ji's wolf-and-otter jest sounds flip its moral still rewards study.)
translations.idiomatic: Crude analogy—sharp point underneath.)

sentences.zh: 是時，曹爽專政，丁謐、鄧颺等輕改法度。

translations.literal: Then Cao Shuang governed alone while Ding Mi and Deng Yang rashly rewrote statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang's cabal rewrote law with Mi and Yang.

sentences.zh: 會有日蝕變，詔羣臣問其得失，濟上疏曰：

translations.literal: A solar eclipse prompted edict assembling ministers on faults—Ji memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: An eclipse summoned debate—Ji wrote:

sentences.zh: 昔大舜佐治，戒在比周；

translations.literal: Great Shun aiding rule warned against factions;
translations.idiomatic: Shun damned cliques;

sentences.zh: 周公輔政，慎於其朋；

translations.literal: Duke Zhou aiding rule was wary of companions;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou feared cozy gangs;

sentences.zh: 齊侯問災，晏嬰對以布惠；

translations.literal: Marquis of Qi asked about calamity—Yan Ying answered spread kindness;
translations.idiomatic: Qi asked omens—Yan Ying preached mercy;

sentences.zh: 魯君問異，臧孫答以緩役。

translations.literal: Lu's lord asked about prodigies—Zangsun answered ease corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Lu asked wonders—Zangsun said lighten labor.

sentences.zh: 應天塞變，乃實人事。

translations.literal: Answering heaven and plugging prodigy truly rests in human deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven follows conduct.

sentences.zh: 今二賊未滅，將士暴露已數十年，男女怨曠，百姓貧苦。

translations.literal: Two rebels still live—troops freeze on campaign decades—men and women long separated—people poor and bitter.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Shu breathe—armies camp forever—homes starve.

sentences.zh: 夫為國法度，惟命世大才，乃能張其綱維以垂於後，豈中下之吏所宜改易哉？

translations.literal: State law belongs to era-making genius who stretches the net for posterity—how may middling clerks rewrite it?
translations.idiomatic: Only founders codify—clerks must not edit.

sentences.zh: 終無益於治，適足傷民，望宜使文武之臣各守其職，率以清平，則和氣祥瑞可感而致也。

translations.literal: It never aids rule—only wounds the people—better civil and martial officers mind their posts steering purity—then harmony and omens arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Meddling hurts farmers—let ministers hold their lanes until auspice returns.

sentences.zh: 劉放字子棄，涿郡人，漢廣陽順王子西鄉侯宏後也。

translations.literal: Liu Fang courtesy Ziji of Zhuo Commandery—descendant of Han Prince Shun of Guangyang's son Marquis Hong of Xixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang, style Ziji from Zhuo—sprung from Prince Hong of Xixiang.

sentences.zh: 歷郡綱紀，舉孝廉。

translations.literal: He served commandery chief clerk and was raised Filial and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: County aide—Filial graduate.

sentences.zh: 遭世大亂，時漁陽王松據其土，放往依之。

translations.literal: Amid great turmoil Wang Song of Yuyang held the territory—Fang joined him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang sheltered under Yuyang's Wang Song.

sentences.zh: 太祖克冀州，放說松曰：

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor took Ji Province Fang urged Song:
translations.idiomatic: Ji fell—Fang briefed Song:

sentences.zh: 往者董卓作逆，英雄並起，阻兵擅命，人自封殖，惟曹公能拔拯危亂，翼戴天子，奉辭伐罪，所向必克。

translations.literal: Once Dong Zhuo rebelled heroes rose—blocking arms and seizing mandates each enriched himself—only Lord Cao pulled the realm from ruin, steadied the Son of Heaven, bore mandate punishing guilt—and conquered wherever he struck.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo's mutiny bred warlords—only Cao Cao saved the throne and struck guilt wherever aimed.

sentences.zh: 以二袁之強，守則淮南冰消，戰則官渡大敗；

translations.literal: Against the two Yuans' might defense melted Huainan like ice—battle broke them at Guandu;
translations.idiomatic: Twin Yuans broke—south froze—north shattered at Guandu;

sentences.zh: 乘勝席捲，將清河朔，威刑既合，大勢以見。

translations.literal: riding victory like a mat scroll he was about to sweep Hebei—awe and law merged—the great tendency stood plain.
translations.idiomatic: Momentum swept north—law and terror fused.

sentences.zh: 速至者漸福，後服者先亡，此乃不俟終日馳騖之時也。

translations.literal: Those swift to join gained blessing—late submitters died first—this was not an hour to idle.
translations.idiomatic: Early birds thrived—late knees drowned—no day to tarry.

sentences.zh: 昔黥布棄南面之尊，仗劍歸漢，誠識廢興之理，審去就之分也。

translations.literal: Qing Bu once threw away southern kingship and sword-in-hand joined Han—seeing rise and fall he knew when to leave or stay.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Bu quit crowns for Han—he read tides.

sentences.zh: 將軍宜投身委命，厚自結納。

translations.literal: You should cast yourself on His mandate and bind ties thickly.
translations.idiomatic: Prostrate yourself—tie tight bonds.

sentences.zh: 松然之。

translations.literal: Song agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Song nodded.

sentences.zh: 會太祖討袁譚於南皮，以書招松，松舉雍奴、泉州、安次以附之。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor attacked Yuan Tan at Nanpi he summoned Song by letter—Song raised Yongnu Quanzhou and Anci to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Nanpi campaign brought letter—Song handed three counties.

sentences.zh: 放為松答太祖書，其文甚麗。

translations.literal: Fang drafted Song's reply—language splendid.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's brush dazzled.

sentences.zh: 太祖既善之，又聞其說，由是遂辟放。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor admired the prose and heard the persuasion—thereby summoned Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao loved the letter—called Fang north.

sentences.zh: 建安十年，與松俱至。

translations.literal: Jian'an tenth year he arrived with Song.
translations.idiomatic: Year ten—Fang rode with Song.

sentences.zh: 太祖大悅，謂放曰：「昔班彪依竇融而有河西之功，今一何相似也！

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor rejoiced telling Fang "Formerly Ban Biao relied on Dou Rong and earned Hexi—how alike today!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao grinned: "Ban Biao and Dou Rong—your mirror!

sentences.zh: 」乃以放參司空軍事，歷主簿記室，出為郃陽、祋祤、

translations.literal: "Thereupon he appointed Fang to Minister of Works military staff, promoted him through chief clerk and secretary, then sent him out as magistrate of Heyang and—
translations.idiomatic: Fang joined the ministry ladder—then county posts at Heyang and—

sentences.zh: 〈祋音都活反。

translations.literal: 〈Note: the graph 祋 is read duò (du-huo reading).〉
translations.idiomatic: (Pronunciation gloss: 祋 reads duò.)

sentences.zh: 祤音詡。〉

translations.literal: Editorial gloss: the commentary supplies the reading xu for this uncommon place-name graph.
translations.idiomatic: Note on pronunciation: read this rare place-name character xu, as indicated in the commentary.

sentences.zh: 贊令。

translations.literal: —magistrate of Zan.
translations.idiomatic: —then magistrate of Zan.

sentences.zh: 魏國既建，與太原孫資俱為秘書郎。

translations.literal: Once Wei state was founded he and Sun Zi of Taiyuan both served Secretary Clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Wei born—Fang and Taiyuan's Sun Zi became secretaries.

sentences.zh: 先是，資亦歷縣令，參丞相軍事。

translations.literal: Earlier Zi too had served county magistrate and joined Chancellor military staff.
translations.idiomatic: Zi had been prefect and staff aide.

sentences.zh: 〈資別傳曰：資字彥龍。

translations.literal: Separate biography of Zi states Zi courtesy Yanlong.
translations.idiomatic: Zi's memoir names him Yanlong.

sentences.zh: 幼而岐嶷，三歲喪二親，長於兄嫂。

translations.literal: Young he showed precocity—age three lost both parents—raised by elder brother and sister-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at three—brother's roof.

sentences.zh: 講業太學，博覽傳記，同郡王允一見而奇之。

translations.literal: Studied Imperial Academy widely reading histories—Wang Yun of same commandery saw him once and marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Academy reader—Wang Yun spotted genius.

sentences.zh: 太祖為司空，又辟資。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor as Minister of Works summoned Zi again.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao as Minister of Works called him twice.

sentences.zh: 會兄為鄉人所害，資手刃報讎，乃將家屬避地河東，故遂不應命。

translations.literal: It happened elder brother was murdered by townsfolk—Zi slew the killer with his own blade—then moved household avoiding to Hedong—therefore never answered summons.
translations.idiomatic: Brother murdered—Zi knifed the killer—fled to Hedong—ignored draft.

sentences.zh: 尋復為本郡所命，以疾辭。

translations.literal: Soon summoned again by native commandery—declined citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Home county tried again—pleaded sick.

sentences.zh: 友人河東賈逵謂資曰：「足下抱逸羣之才，值舊邦傾覆，主將殷勤，千里延頸，宜崇古賢桑梓之義。

translations.literal: Friend Jia Kui of Hedong told Zi "You harbor talents surpassing the herd yet homeland overturns—your commander earnest neck craned a thousand li—you ought honor ancient worthy's duty to native soil.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui urged: homeland burns—lord beckons—duty calls.

sentences.zh: 而久盤桓，拒違君命，斯猶曜和璧於秦王之庭，而塞以連城之價耳。

translations.literal: Yet long lingering refusing lord commands is like flashing He shi jade in Qin king's court yet blocking even linked-city price.
translations.idiomatic: Lingering is flashing priceless jade yet refusing sale.

sentences.zh: 竊為足下不取也！

translations.literal: Your servant privately thinks you ought not choose thus!
translations.idiomatic: Do not insult yourself so!

sentences.zh: 」資感其言，遂往應之。

translations.literal: "Zi moved by words went to answer summons.
translations.idiomatic: Zi yielded—rode to serve.

sentences.zh: 到署功曹，舉計吏。

translations.literal: Arriving appointed merit clerk raised accounting clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Posted merit aide—sent up accountant.

sentences.zh: 尚書令荀彧見資，歎曰：「北州承喪亂已久，謂其賢智零落，今日乃復見孫計君乎！

translations.literal: Minister Director Xun Yu seeing Zi sighed "Northlands long wasted by chaos—I thought worthies vanished—today I see Clerk Sun again!
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu gasped: north in ruins—yet Sun Zi lives!

sentences.zh: 」表留以為尚書郎。

translations.literal: "Memorialized to retain him as Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yu kept him at Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 辭以家難，得還河東。〉

translations.literal: He declined citing household tragedy allowed return Hedong.)
translations.idiomatic: Family grief sent him back east.)

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，放、資轉為左右丞。

translations.literal: When Wen Emperor ascended Fang and Zi became Left and Right Assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Pi named them left and right aides.

sentences.zh: 數月，放徙為令。

translations.literal: Several months later Fang shifted to Director.
translations.idiomatic: Months on—Fang became director.

sentences.zh: 黃初初，改秘書為中書，以放為監，資為令，各加給事中；

translations.literal: Early Huangchu Secretariat renamed Palace Secretariat—Fang Supervisor Zi Director—each added Palace Consultant;
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu renamed the bureau—Fang supervised—Zi directed—both consultants;

sentences.zh: 放賜爵關內侯，資為關中侯，遂掌機密。

translations.literal: Fang enfeoffed secondary marquis within passes Zi Guanzhong marquis—thereafter grasped secrets.
translations.idiomatic: Noble stipends followed—pair held cipher.

sentences.zh: 三年，放進爵魏壽亭侯，資關內侯。

translations.literal: Third year Fang advanced village marquis of Weishou Zi secondary marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Year three boosted titles.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，尤見寵任，同加散騎常侍；

translations.literal: Ming Emperor enthroned favored them doubly—both added Palace Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Rui adored both—added attendants;

sentences.zh: 進放爵西鄉侯，資樂陽亭侯。

translations.literal: Fang advanced village marquis of Xixiang Zi village marquis of Leyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fiefs widened—Xixiang and Leyang.

sentences.zh: 〈資別傳曰：諸葛亮出在南鄭，時議者以為可因發大兵，就討之，帝意亦然，以問資。

translations.literal: Separate biography of Zi: Zhuge Liang marched from Nan—debate favored striking with mass army—Emperor agreed—questioned Zi.
translations.idiomatic: Li's Nan drive tempted grand assault—Rui asked Zi.

sentences.zh: 資曰：〉

translations.literal: Zi said:
translations.idiomatic: Zi answered:

sentences.zh: 昔武皇帝征南鄭，取張魯，陽平之役，危而後濟。

translations.literal: Formerly Martial Emperor campaigned Nan taking Zhang Lu—Yangping battle perilous before succeeding.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Di took Hanzhong through Yangping's nightmare.

sentences.zh: 又自往拔出夏侯淵軍，數言『南鄭直為天獄，中斜谷道為五百里石穴耳』，言其深險，喜出淵軍之辭也。

translations.literal: He personally extracted Xiahou Yuan's army repeatedly saying "Nanping is heaven's prison central Xie Valley road merely five hundred li stone tunnel"—speaking its depth peril rejoicing words escaping Yuan's army.
translations.idiomatic: He called Nanping heaven's jail—Xie Gorge five hundred li of stone—relief when Yuan escaped.

sentences.zh: 又武皇帝聖於用兵，察蜀賊棲於山岩，視吳虜竄於江湖，皆橈而避之，不責將士之力，不爭一朝之忿，誠所謂見勝而戰，知難而退也。

translations.literal: Moreover Martial Emperor sage in employing arms saw Shu bandits nesting mountain cliffs Wu foes fleeing rivers lakes—both times bent aside avoiding them—not demanding soldiers' utmost nor contesting morning wrath—truly so-called seeing victory then fighting knowing hardship then retreating.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Di dodged Shu cliffs and Wu rivers—never wasted wrath—won when safe—quit when steep.

sentences.zh: 今若進軍就南鄭討亮，道既險阻，計用精兵又轉運鎮守南方四州遏禦水賊，凡用十五六萬人，必當復更有所發興。

translations.literal: Now marching on Nan to strike Liang road already perilous reckoning elite troops plus convoys guarding four southern provinces blocking river bandits totals hundred fifty sixty thousand—surely further levies follow.
translations.idiomatic: Nan assault needs elites plus convoys plus four southern garrisons—sixteen myriads—and more.

sentences.zh: 天下騷動，費力廣大，此誠陛下所宜深慮。

translations.literal: Realm stirs effort vast—truly what Your Majesty ought ponder deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Empire quakes—think twice.

sentences.zh: 夫守戰之力，力役參倍。

translations.literal: Defense versus assault labor triples.
translations.idiomatic: Holding costs thrice attacking.

sentences.zh: 但以今日見兵，分命大將據諸要險，威足以震攝強寇，鎮靜疆埸，將士虎睡，百姓無事。

translations.literal: Yet using present visible troops assigning great generals holding key narrows awe suffices to cow strong bandits quiet borders generals tiger-sleep common people untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: Split today's host across chokepoints—foes freeze—people farm.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，中國日盛，吳蜀二虜必自罷弊。

translations.literal: Within several years Central Plains daily flourishes Wu Shu two villains surely exhaust themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Years pass—heartland swells—Wu-Shu rot alone.

sentences.zh: 〈帝由是止。

translations.literal: (Emperor therefore stopped.)
